AABB.description: An Axis-Aligned Bounding Box defined by a minimum and maximum Vector3 corner. All edges are parallel to the world axes, making AABB overlap tests extremely fast. AABBs are used throughout Doriax for mesh bounds queries, frustum culling, and physics broad-phase.

members.contains: Returns `true` if this AABB fully contains the given point or box.
members.distance: Distance from a point to the nearest surface of this box. Returns `0` if the point is inside.
members.finite: An AABB can be in one of three states: null (undefined, no extent), finite (normal bounding box), or infinite (the entire space). Intersection tests respect these states.
members.getCenter: `getCenter()` returns the midpoint. `getSize()` returns `max - min`. `getHalfSize()` returns half the size — convenient for physics and intersection tests.
members.getCorner: `getCorner()` returns one corner, named by `AABB.CornerEnum` (`FAR_LEFT_BOTTOM`, `NEAR_RIGHT_TOP`, and so on). `getCorners()` returns all eight, in the order of those enum values. Lua gets them as a table of copies, so `corners[c + 1]` is `getCorner(c)`. Only a finite box has corners: in C++ `getCorners()` asserts on a null or infinite box, and Lua gets an empty table.
members.getCorners: `getCorner()` returns one corner, named by `AABB.CornerEnum` (`FAR_LEFT_BOTTOM`, `NEAR_RIGHT_TOP`, and so on). `getCorners()` returns all eight, in the order of those enum values. Lua gets them as a table of copies, so `corners[c + 1]` is `getCorner(c)`. Only a finite box has corners: in C++ `getCorners()` asserts on a null or infinite box, and Lua gets an empty table.
members.getHalfSize: `getCenter()` returns the midpoint. `getSize()` returns `max - min`. `getHalfSize()` returns half the size — convenient for physics and intersection tests.
members.getOBB: Converts this AABB to an OBB with axis-aligned orientation.
members.getSize: `getCenter()` returns the midpoint. `getSize()` returns `max - min`. `getHalfSize()` returns half the size — convenient for physics and intersection tests.
members.infinite: An AABB can be in one of three states: null (undefined, no extent), finite (normal bounding box), or infinite (the entire space). Intersection tests respect these states.
members.intersection: Returns the AABB formed by the overlap of this box and `b2`. Returns a null AABB if there is no overlap.
members.intersects: Overlap tests against other volumes or a point.
members.maximum: The two corner points of the box in world space.
members.merge: Expands this AABB to also contain `rhs` or the given `point`.
members.minimum: The two corner points of the box in world space.
members.null: An AABB can be in one of three states: null (undefined, no extent), finite (normal bounding box), or infinite (the entire space). Intersection tests respect these states.
members.scale: Scales the AABB from its centre by the given factor.
members.setExtents: Sets both minimum and maximum in one call.
members.squaredDistance: Distance from a point to the nearest surface of this box. Returns `0` if the point is inside.
members.transform: Transforms the AABB by `matrix`. Note: an AABB after transformation is re-fitted, which may be larger than the OBB would be.

Action.description: Base class for all time-driven actions in Doriax. Actions are managed by ActionSystem, which advances them each frame. You typically do not instantiate `Action` directly; instead you use concrete subclasses:

members.getTimeCount: Returns the action's internal time counter in seconds, from `0` at the start to the action's total duration at completion.
members.isPaused: Query the current playback state. An action is running if it has been started and has not yet completed, been paused, or been stopped.
members.isRunning: Query the current playback state. An action is running if it has been started and has not yet completed, been paused, or been stopped.
members.isStopped: Query the current playback state. An action is running if it has been started and has not yet completed, been paused, or been stopped.
members.ownedTarget: When `true`, the action takes ownership of its target entity — the target is automatically destroyed when the action is destroyed. Useful for fire-and-forget effects where both the action and the visual entity should be cleaned up together.
members.randomStart: Where the action starts, in seconds: `startOffset` starts it that far in, and `randomStart` at a random time of its duration instead, so copies of the same animation do not move in sync. Both apply when the action starts from stopped, not when it resumes from a pause, also for an action that an Animation plays. The editor preview always starts at the beginning.
members.restart: Plays the action again from the beginning: a running or paused action is stopped and started again in the same update (its `onStop` and `onStart` events both fire), and a stopped one just starts.
members.setTarget: Assigns the Object or entity that this action modifies. Most actions require a target to be set before `start()` is called.
members.speed: Playback speed multiplier. `1.0` is normal speed, `2.0` plays twice as fast, `0.5` in slow motion. Negative values play the action in reverse (where supported by the subclass).
members.startOffset: Where the action starts, in seconds: `startOffset` starts it that far in, and `randomStart` at a random time of its duration instead, so copies of the same animation do not move in sync. Both apply when the action starts from stopped, not when it resumes from a pause, also for an action that an Animation plays. The editor preview always starts at the beginning.
members.weight: Blend weight (`0.0`–`1.0`) for this action's contribution when several actions drive the same target. When multiple skeletal clips animate the same bone, `ActionSystem` combines their sampled poses as a weight-normalized average rather than letting the last one win, which is what makes crossfades smooth.

AdMob.description: Google Mobile Ads on Android and iOS: banner, interstitial, rewarded, rewarded interstitial and app open ads, plus Google's consent form (User Messaging Platform). Exports include the SDK only when Google AdMob is enabled in the project's Android or iOS settings. Everywhere else the calls still compile and run, and report `errorNotAvailable` through their events.

members.getConsentStatus: The consent state Google has stored. `canRequestAds()` is true once the consent allows ad requests, including consent from an earlier launch. Without AdMob in the build they return `UNKNOWN` and `false`.
members.initialize: Starts Google Mobile Ads with the request settings made so far. `onInitialized` fires when it is ready, and `isInitialized()` is true from then on. Call it once consent allows ad requests (`canRequestAds()`), and load the first ads in `onInitialized`.
members.isPrivacyOptionsRequired: When `isPrivacyOptionsRequired()` is true, the game must offer a way back to the consent form, such as a Privacy button in its settings, which calls `showPrivacyOptionsForm()`. Closing the form reports through `onConsentUpdated`.
members.loadBannerAd: Loads a banner and shows it over the game as soon as it loads, replacing any banner already there. `onAdLoaded(BANNER)` or `onAdFailedToLoad(BANNER, ...)` reports the result. An `ADAPTIVE` banner takes the screen width when it loads, so load it again after the screen rotates.
members.openAdInspector: Opens Google's Ad Inspector, which shows the requests and mediation results of each ad unit. It only opens on a test device. `onAdInspectorClosed(errorCode, message)` fires when it closes.
members.requestConsent: Updates the user's consent information and shows Google's consent form when the user still has to answer, as Google's policies require in the EEA, the UK, Switzerland and some US states. Call it at every launch, before `initialize()`. `onConsentUpdated(errorCode, message)` reports the result, with `errorCode` 0 on success. Without AdMob in the build it reports `errorNotAvailable`.
members.resetConsent: Forgets the stored consent, so the next `requestConsent()` asks again. Meant for testing.
members.setAppVolume: Volume of video ads relative to the game, from 0 to 1, and whether they play muted. Match them to the game's own volume settings.
members.setConsentDebugGeography: Makes the next `requestConsent()` on a test device act as if the user were in that region, to see the consent form from anywhere. Defaults to `DISABLED`.
members.setServerSideVerificationOptions: Data passed to the server-side verification callback of rewarded ads, which lets your server confirm a reward before granting it. It applies to the rewarded and rewarded interstitial ads shown after the call.
members.setTestDeviceIds: Devices that get test ads, by the hashed ID Google Mobile Ads prints to the device log (Logcat or the Xcode console). The consent debug settings also apply only to these devices. In Lua, pass a table of strings.

AlphaAction.description: Animates the `alpha` (opacity) property of its target object from a start value to an end value over a fixed duration.

members.setAction: Configures the tween. `startAlpha` and `endAlpha` are opacity values in `[0, 1]`. `duration` is in seconds.

Angle.description: A static utility class providing angle conversion functions between degrees, radians, and Doriax's default unit, which is controlled by `Engine::useDegrees`.

members.defaultToDeg: Convert from the engine's default unit to radians or degrees.
members.defaultToRad: Convert from the engine's default unit to radians or degrees.
members.degToDefault: Convert a value in radians or degrees to the engine's current default angle unit. If `Engine::useDegrees` is `true`, `radToDefault()` converts radians → degrees and `degToDefault()` is a no-op.
members.degToRad: Direct conversion between radians and degrees, independent of the engine's `useDegrees` setting.
members.radToDefault: Convert a value in radians or degrees to the engine's current default angle unit. If `Engine::useDegrees` is `true`, `radToDefault()` converts radians → degrees and `degToDefault()` is a no-op.
members.radToDeg: Direct conversion between radians and degrees, independent of the engine's `useDegrees` setting.

Animation.description: A timeline-based animation composed of `ActionFrame` entries. Each frame schedules an Action to run against a target entity at a specific time offset, for a specific duration. Frames can overlap to create parallel tweens, producing complex multi-property animations.

members.blendWeight: The clip's current blend weight (`0.0`–`1.0`). When several clips animate the same skeleton, each bone's final pose is the weight-normalized average of the running clips, so weights let you layer or crossfade animations smoothly.
members.clearActionFrames: Removes all frames from the timeline. This method is not exposed to Lua.
members.defaultFadeTime: The crossfade duration (in seconds) used by Model::playAnimation() when it is called without an explicit fade time. Authored per-clip and saved with the scene — set it in the Properties window (AnimationComponent → Fade time) or in code. Defaults to `0.15`.
members.duration: Total length of the animation in seconds. When loading a model, this is set automatically from the GLTF data. The getter and setter are not exposed to Lua; Lua-created sequences derive their duration from their action frames.
members.fadeIn: Crossfade primitives that ramp the clip's blendWeight over `duration` seconds.
members.fadeOut: Crossfade primitives that ramp the clip's blendWeight over `duration` seconds.
members.getActionFrame: Returns a reference to the ActionFrame at the given zero-based index.
members.getActionFrameSize: Returns the number of frames currently in the timeline.
members.loop: When `true`, the animation restarts from the beginning after playing to completion.
members.name: Inherited from: EntityHandle
members.ownedActions: When `true`, all child Action entities referenced by the animation's frames are destroyed when the animation is destroyed. Useful for animations built entirely in code.
members.setActionFrameDuration: Modify the start time or duration of an existing frame by index. Setting `duration` to `0` (or lower) switches the frame to auto: it follows the action's own duration.
members.setActionFrameEntity: Replace the action entity for a given frame.
members.setActionFrameStartTime: Modify the start time or duration of an existing frame by index. Setting `duration` to `0` (or lower) switches the frame to auto: it follows the action's own duration.

Base64.description: Static helpers for encoding and decoding binary data as base64 strings. Useful for embedding small payloads in JSON/YAML or for network/save serialization.

Body2D.description: `Body2D` is the 2D rigid-body handle built on top of the Box2D v3 physics library. Obtain one by calling `object.getBody2D()`. After creating shapes and setting properties, call `load()` to register the body with the physics world. The body position is synchronized with the parent Object transform automatically each physics step.

members.angle: The body's own pose in world space, read from and written straight to the simulation, and the only way to place a body from `onFixedUpdate`. Setting either also updates the entity Object transform so rendering follows and the next step does not undo the move. Both wake the body. Box2D owns only X and Y, so the Transform's Z is left untouched.
members.angularDamping: Drag coefficients that slow down translation and rotation over time. Values in `[0, ∞)`. Zero means no damping.
members.angularVelocity: Current angular velocity in radians per second (regardless of `Engine::useDegrees`).
members.applyForce: Applies a force (in Newtons) at a given world-space `point`. Pass `wake = true` to activate a sleeping body.
members.applyForceToCenter: Applies a force at the body's center of mass; produces linear acceleration but no torque.
members.applyLinearImpulse: Instantaneous velocity changes (Δv = impulse / mass). Prefer impulses over forces for one-shot events like jumps.
members.applyLinearImpulseToCenter: Instantaneous velocity changes (Δv = impulse / mass). Prefer impulses over forces for one-shot events like jumps.
members.applyMassFromShapes: Recomputes mass and inertia from the attached shapes' density values. Call after changing `setShapeDensity` at runtime.
members.applyTorque: Applies a rotational force. Positive values spin counter-clockwise.
members.bullet: Enables continuous collision detection (CCD) for fast-moving objects that might tunnel through thin geometry in a single time step.
members.createBoxShape: Creates a rectangular polygon shape with corner at the entity's local origin. Returns the shape index (0-based).
members.createCapsuleShape: Creates a capsule defined by two center points and a radius. Good for characters and rounded projectiles.
members.createCenteredBoxShape: Creates a rectangular polygon centered at `(width/2, height/2)` relative to the entity origin. The second overload allows an explicit center offset and pre-rotation.
members.createChainShape: Creates a chain of connected edge segments. When `loop` is `true`, the last point connects back to the first forming a closed boundary.
members.createCircleShape: Creates a circle shape at `center` (in local space) with the given `radius`.
members.createPolygonShape: Creates a convex hull from the given vertices. Box2D requires the shape to be convex; provide vertices in counter-clockwise order.
members.createRoundedBoxShape: Creates a rounded rectangle (box with chamfered corners). `radius` specifies the corner rounding amount.
members.createSegmentShape: Creates a line segment between `point1` and `point2`. It collides on both sides and has no mass. For outlines made of many edges, use a chain instead.
members.createTilemapShape: Creates a polygon shape built from the tiles of the Tilemap on the same entity. Tiles that touch are merged, first into rows and then into blocks of rows with the same width, and each block becomes one box. Tiles whose rect has `collision` set to `false` are left out.
members.fixedRotation: When `true`, the body cannot rotate. Useful for top-down characters that should always stay upright. It is the rotation lock of setMotionLocks.
members.getAttachedObject: Returns the Object whose entity owns this body.
members.getBodyContacts: Returns currently active contact manifolds for the entire body or for a specific shape. Useful for manual overlap queries without subscribing to per-frame events. `getShapeContacts` doesn't work on chain shapes; use `getBodyContacts` for those.
members.getPointsToMeterScale: Returns the pixels-to-meters conversion scale used by Box2D. The physics simulation uses SI units (meters/kg/seconds); divide pixel distances by this value before passing them to physics methods, or use the engine's automatic scaling.
members.getShapeContacts: Returns currently active contact manifolds for the entire body or for a specific shape. Useful for manual overlap queries without subscribing to per-frame events. `getShapeContacts` doesn't work on chain shapes; use `getBodyContacts` for those.
members.gravityScale: Multiplier applied to global gravity for this body. `0` means the body is unaffected by gravity; negative values invert gravity.
members.linearDamping: Drag coefficients that slow down translation and rotation over time. Values in `[0, ∞)`. Zero means no damping.
members.linearVelocity: Current velocity of the center of mass in points per second — the same units as positions, so `setLinearVelocity(Vector2(300, 0))` crosses 300 points in one second. Forces and impulses are not converted: they stay in Box2D units (Newtons on the meter-scaled body).
members.load: Registers all shapes with the Box2D world and activates the body. Must be called after creating shapes. Call again to rebuild the body after runtime shape changes.
members.mass: Computed mass and moment of inertia. Updated automatically when applyMassFromShapes is called.
members.position: The body's own pose in world space, read from and written straight to the simulation, and the only way to place a body from `onFixedUpdate`. Setting either also updates the entity Object transform so rendering follows and the next step does not undo the move. Both wake the body. Box2D owns only X and Y, so the Transform's Z is left untouched.
members.removeAllShapes: Removes all shapes from the body. Call load again after adding new shapes.
members.rotationalInertia: Computed mass and moment of inertia. Updated automatically when applyMassFromShapes is called.
members.setBitsFilter: Configures collision filtering using bitmasks. A body collides with another only if `(a.category & b.mask) != 0` and `(b.category & a.mask) != 0`.
members.setMotionLocks: Stops the body moving along world X, along world Y, or rotating. A locked axis ignores gravity, forces and contacts; the others move as usual. A character that only falls, or a piston that only slides sideways, is one lock away. The rotation lock is fixedRotation. The locks live on the loaded body, so set them after load.
members.setShapeContactEvents: Enable specific collision event callbacks for a shape. See PhysicsSystem events and Events manual.
members.setShapeEnableHitEvents: Enable specific collision event callbacks for a shape. See PhysicsSystem events and Events manual.
members.setShapePreSolveEvents: Enable specific collision event callbacks for a shape. See PhysicsSystem events and Events manual.
members.setShapeRollingResistance: Both have the same two overloads as friction, and are fields of each shape in the editor (Rolling Resistance, Tangent Speed). A chain takes them on every edge.
members.setShapeSensor: Turns a shape into a sensor: an overlap-only shape that never pushes anything and is reported through `beginSensorContact2D` / `endSensorContact2D` instead of the contact events. Pickups, triggers and hurt zones are the typical use. A sensor always has its sensor events enabled, so the callbacks arrive without further setup; two sensors never report each other. The flag is also a checkbox on the shape in the editor (Sensor) and the `shapeSensor` property in Lua. Box2D has no live toggle for it, so changing it rebuilds the body's shapes on the next physics step.
members.setShapeSensorEvents: Enable specific collision event callbacks for a shape. See PhysicsSystem events and Events manual.
members.setShapeTangentSpeed: Both have the same two overloads as friction, and are fields of each shape in the editor (Rolling Resistance, Tangent Speed). A chain takes them on every edge.
members.type: Sets the body simulation mode. See BodyType. Must be set before calling load or changed at runtime by re-loading the body.

Body3D.description: `Body3D` is the 3D rigid-body handle built on top of the Jolt Physics library. Obtain one by calling `object.getBody3D()`. Create one or more shapes, set the body type and material properties, then call `load()` to register with the physics world. The body transform is synchronized with the parent Object each physics step.

members.angularVelocity: Current velocity vectors. Linear velocity is in world units/second; angular velocity is in radians/second around each world axis.
members.applyAngularImpulse: Instantaneous angular velocity change. Useful for spinning objects on impact.
members.applyBuoyancyImpulse: Simulates buoyancy for a body partially submerged in a fluid. Returns `true` if the body intersects the water plane. Only a dynamic body is pushed, and a sleeping one wakes up. Call once per physics step with the water plane data. A body in a Water gets this every fixed step from its buoyancy settings, so call it yourself only for fluids that are not a Water component.
members.applyForce: Applies a force in Newtons each simulation step. The single-argument overload applies force at the center of mass (no torque). The two-argument overload applies force at a world-space point, potentially generating torque.
members.applyImpulse: Instantaneous velocity change. Prefer impulses over forces for one-shot events (jumps, explosions, hits).
members.applyTorque: Applies a torque (Nm) to rotate the body. The vector direction defines the rotation axis (right-hand rule).
members.buoyancy: How the body floats in a Water. `buoyancy` compares the water's density to the body's: `1` is neutral, more floats and less sinks. `0` (the default) ignores the water. `waterDrag` is how much the water slows the body down, and `waterAngularDrag` how much it slows its rotation.
members.categoryBitsFilter: Collision layer filtering bitmasks. A collision occurs only when `(a.category & b.mask) != 0`.
members.collideKinematicVsNonDynamic: When `true`, this kinematic body generates collision reports against static and other kinematic bodies (normally skipped for performance).
members.collisionGroupID: Group index for disabling self-collision within a group (e.g. ragdoll bones).
members.createBoxShape: Creates a solid box collider. Returns the shape index. The offset overload positions the shape relative to the entity origin.
members.createCapsuleShape: Creates a vertical capsule (hemisphere-capped cylinder). Standard character controller shape.
members.createConvexHullShape: Creates a convex hull from the mesh vertices (no-argument form) or from explicit vertices. Must be convex; Jolt computes the hull automatically.
members.createCylinderShape: Upright cylinder collider. Less stable than capsules on uneven ground; prefer capsules for characters.
members.createHeightFieldShape: Creates a height-field collider sized to the terrain mesh in the entity. Used with the Terrain class. `samplesSize` controls the resolution grid. setShapeBitsPerSample sets how precisely each height is stored.
members.createMeshShape: Creates a static triangle-mesh collider. Mesh shapes can only be STATIC. Use convex hull for dynamic objects. For a large mesh, setShapeBuildQuality trades query speed for a faster build.
members.createSphereShape: Creates a sphere collider. Spheres are the cheapest shape to simulate.
members.createTaperedCapsuleShape: Capsule with different radii at each end. Useful for cones, bullets, and stylised characters.
members.friction: Surface material properties shared across all shapes on this body. Friction `[0, ∞)` controls sliding resistance; restitution `[0, 1]` controls bounciness.
members.getCenterOfMassPosition: Returns the world-space position of the center of mass, which may differ from the entity origin if shapes are offset.
members.getPointVelocity: Returns the velocity of a world-space point on the body, including the contribution of angular velocity. Use for precise impact and dragging calculations.
members.getSubmergedVolume: How much of the body lies below a fluid surface, given as a plane through `surfacePosition` whose `surfaceNormal` points up, out of the fluid. Returns a SubmergedVolume3D with the volumes, the submerged `fraction` and the centre of buoyancy. It only reads the body, so it applies no force: use it for gameplay, such as a splash when `fraction` first rises above `0`, or a sinking state once it nears `1`. It works for any body type, but not for a body with a mesh or height-field shape, which has no volume: that call logs an error and returns zeros.
members.gravityFactor: Scales the global gravity for this body. `0` = gravity-free, `2` = double gravity.
members.linearVelocity: Current velocity vectors. Linear velocity is in world units/second; angular velocity is in radians/second around each world axis.
members.load: Registers the body and all its shapes with the Jolt physics world. Must be called after defining shapes. Re-call if shapes change at runtime.
members.maskBitsFilter: Collision layer filtering bitmasks. A collision occurs only when `(a.category & b.mask) != 0`.
members.mass: The body's mass in kilograms. The setter scales the inertia by the same factor, so a body made heavier also gets harder to spin. Set it after calling load; see setMass. The getter returns the mass the body has now, including a change from `setMass` or setOverrideMassAndInertia; for a static body it returns the mass its shapes would give.
members.position: The body's own pose in world space, read from and written straight to the simulation, and the only way to place a body from `onFixedUpdate`. Setting either also updates the entity Object transform so rendering follows and the next step does not undo the move. Both wake the body.
members.restitution: Surface material properties shared across all shapes on this body. Friction `[0, ∞)` controls sliding resistance; restitution `[0, 1]` controls bounciness.
members.rotation: The body's own pose in world space, read from and written straight to the simulation, and the only way to place a body from `onFixedUpdate`. Setting either also updates the entity Object transform so rendering follows and the next step does not undo the move. Both wake the body.
members.sensor: When `true`, the body acts as a trigger volume: overlapping bodies generate contact events but no physical impulse is applied.
members.setAllowedDOFs: Constrain which degrees of freedom the body can move in.
members.setAllowedDOFs2DPlane: Constrain which degrees of freedom the body can move in.
members.setAllowedDOFsAll: Constrain which degrees of freedom the body can move in.
members.setAngularVelocityClamped: Velocity setters that clamp the new value to the body's configured speed limits (set in Jolt body settings). Safer for kinematic controllers.
members.setLinearVelocityClamped: Velocity setters that clamp the new value to the body's configured speed limits (set in Jolt body settings). Safer for kinematic controllers.
members.setMass: `setMass` changes only the live body: a body reload computes the mass from the shapes again. To keep a mass, set it through the shape density or the solid-box override.
members.setOverrideMassAndInertia: `setMass` changes only the live body: a body reload computes the mass from the shapes again. To keep a mass, set it through the shape density or the solid-box override.
members.setShapeBitsPerSample: How many bits a height-field shape stores for each height, from `1` to `16` (default `8`). The heights are kept in blocks of samples, and the bits divide each block's own height range, so 8 bits already give small steps on gentle ground. More bits make collision follow steep terrain closer and take more memory. The shape is rebuilt on the next update. In the editor it is Bits Per Sample on a heightfield shape.
members.setShapeBuildQuality: How a mesh shape builds its collision tree: see Shape3DBuildQuality. The default favors runtime performance, which suits level geometry built once. `FAVOR_BUILD_SPEED` makes a large mesh load sooner, for example on the web, at a cost on every collision and ray cast against it. The shape is rebuilt on the next update. In the editor it is Build Quality on a mesh shape.
members.setShapeDensity: Sets the density (kg/m³) used to compute mass. Call after adding shapes and before load, or call load again after runtime changes.
members.type: Simulation mode. See BodyType. Can be changed at runtime to switch between, e.g., KINEMATIC and DYNAMIC.

BundleManager.description: A registry for reusable bundles — prefab-like groups of entities that can be spawned into any Scene at runtime. A bundle is authored in the editor and saved as a `.bundle` file (see Bundles).

members.clearAll: Removes all registered bundles and all tracked instances. Used by the editor when resetting state.
members.createBundle: Spawns an instance of a registered bundle into a scene and returns the root entity of the new hierarchy, or a null entity if the name/ID is not found or the factory fails.
members.destroyAllInstances: Destroys every tracked bundle instance belonging to `scene`, calling the appropriate destroyer for each. An instance spawned under another goes with it. C++-only; useful when tearing a scene down manually.
members.destroyBundle: Destroys a bundle instance by its root entity. Its scripts stop first, then every entity the spawn created is removed together with anything parented under the instance since (children first, then the root). A bundle spawned under the instance goes through its own `destroyBundle` before that. The entity the instance was parented to is not touched. If the bundle was registered with a custom destroyer, that is called instead of the default destruction. Returns `false` if `rootEntity` is not a tracked bundle root. Note the argument order: scene first, then the root entity.
members.getBundleId: Look up a bundle's numeric ID by name, or its name by ID. Returns `0` / `""` if not found.
members.getBundleName: Look up a bundle's numeric ID by name, or its name by ID. Returns `0` / `""` if not found.
members.getBundleNames: Returns all registered bundle names, in registration order. Use the `bundleCount` property (Lua) or `getBundleCount()` (C++) for the count.
members.isBundleLoaded: For an instance placed in a scene with On Demand ticked (see Instances loaded on demand), whose scene starts with only its root. `loadBundle` creates the bundle's members under that root and starts their scripts, as `createBundle` does for a spawned instance; it returns `true` when the instance is loaded, also when it already was, and `false` for an entity that is not an on-demand instance or whose bundle is not registered. `unloadBundle` stops the members' scripts and removes them with anything parented under them since; the root, its components, its own scripts and the children its scene gave it stay, so the instance can be loaded again. `isBundleLoaded` answers whether the members are there: always for an instance placed without On Demand or spawned with `createBundle`.
members.isStopping: Returns `true` while `destroyBundle` stops the scripts of that entity. A `start` callback skips such entities, so a script that spawns a bundle from its destructor does not restart what is being destroyed. C++-only.
members.loadBundle: For an instance placed in a scene with On Demand ticked (see Instances loaded on demand), whose scene starts with only its root. `loadBundle` creates the bundle's members under that root and starts their scripts, as `createBundle` does for a spawned instance; it returns `true` when the instance is loaded, also when it already was, and `false` for an entity that is not an on-demand instance or whose bundle is not registered. `unloadBundle` stops the members' scripts and removes them with anything parented under them since; the root, its components, its own scripts and the children its scene gave it stay, so the instance can be loaded again. `isBundleLoaded` answers whether the members are there: always for an instance placed without On Demand or spawned with `createBundle`.
members.registerBundle: Registers a named bundle factory. The `factory` receives the target `Scene*` and a root `Entity`, and must return `true` on success. On failure (or if the factory throws), `createBundle` does not record an instance and rolls back entities created during the call. Void-returning callables are still accepted and treated as success.
members.setScriptCallbacks: Sets how spawned instances start and stop their scripts: `start` runs every script of the scene that has not started yet, and `stop` the scripts of one entity. By default only Lua scripts run. The generated `main.cpp` passes the project's `initScripts` and `cleanupEntityScripts`, and the editor sets its own for Play, so you only call this when running the engine without the generated code. C++-only.
members.unloadBundle: For an instance placed in a scene with On Demand ticked (see Instances loaded on demand), whose scene starts with only its root. `loadBundle` creates the bundle's members under that root and starts their scripts, as `createBundle` does for a spawned instance; it returns `true` when the instance is loaded, also when it already was, and `false` for an entity that is not an on-demand instance or whose bundle is not registered. `unloadBundle` stops the members' scripts and removes them with anything parented under them since; the root, its components, its own scripts and the children its scene gave it stay, so the instance can be loaded again. `isBundleLoaded` answers whether the members are there: always for an instance placed without On Demand or spawned with `createBundle`.

Button.description: An interactive UI button widget. `Button` extends Image with four visual states — normal, hovered, pressed, and disabled — each of which can have a distinct texture or tint colour. An optional text label can be embedded inside the button.

members.disabled: When `true`, the button ignores pointer events and displays with `colorDisabled` / `textureDisabled`. Use to grey out unavailable actions.
members.focusable: When `false`, keys and gamepads leave this button alone: the arrow keys, the d-pad, and the left stick skip it, and Enter, Space, or the A button never press it, so it can only be clicked. Turn it off on a button the focus shouldn't reach, like a HUD button in the same scene as a menu. Hidden and disabled buttons are always skipped.
members.getLabelObject: Returns a handle to the child Text entity. Useful for advanced label manipulation such as alignment or size.
members.hasLabel: Returns `true` if a label child entity has been created for this button.
members.isFocused: Returns `true` while this button has the focus, even when the mouse has hidden it. A click also gives a button the focus, but keys and gamepads only use it once a script has called setFocus.
members.label: The text displayed inside the button. Setting a non-empty label automatically creates a child Text entity. Font and colour apply to that label text. The button's 9-patch margins do not clip the label, but a parent that clips the button still clips it.
members.onPress: `onPress` fires when the mouse button is pressed over the button element, or when Enter, Space, or the gamepad A button is pressed while the button has the focus. `onRelease` fires when that press ends, even if the pointer has left the button. For a click, use the `onClick` event of the button's UIComponent.
members.onRelease: `onPress` fires when the mouse button is pressed over the button element, or when Enter, Space, or the gamepad A button is pressed while the button has the focus. `onRelease` fires when that press ends, even if the pointer has left the button. For a click, use the `onClick` event of the button's UIComponent.
members.setFocus: Moves the keyboard and gamepad focus to this button and shows it, so Enter, Space, or the A button presses it. Call it when a menu opens to start on its main button: keys and gamepads stay with gameplay until a button has the focus. A button with focusable turned off takes the focus but doesn't show it or react to those keys.
members.stateColors: Per-state tint colours multiplied with the current state texture. Use these to create hover and press effects with a single texture. The current state colour replaces the colour of the button's UIComponent, so change `colorNormal` rather than the image colour.
members.statetextures: Assigns a unique texture for each interaction state. If not set, all states use the base texture from Image tinted by the state colour. Whenever the button loads or changes state, the state texture replaces the image texture, so change the button's look with `setTextureNormal`, which sets both, rather than `setTexture`.
members.transitions: A hovered or pressed button grows by `scaleHovered` or `scalePressed` (`1.1` is 10% bigger), around its pivot, so set the pivot to `(0.5, 0.5)` to grow it from the middle. With a `transitionTime` in seconds, the state colour and scale change over that time when the pointer enters, leaves, presses or releases the button, instead of at once. Textures still swap at once.

Camera.description: `Camera` defines the viewpoint from which the scene is rendered. It supports both orthographic (2D) and perspective (3D) projection, a look-at target, manual navigation helpers (walk, slide, orbit), and render-to-texture via an internal `Framebuffer`.

members.activate: Makes this camera the active camera in its scene. Equivalent to calling `scene.setCamera(this)`.
members.aspect: Width-to-height ratio for perspective projection. In auto-resize mode the engine updates this automatically.
members.autoResize: When `true` (default), the projection is automatically recalculated when the canvas size changes. Disable if you manage the projection matrix manually.
members.bottomClip: Orthographic frustum extents. Set via setOrtho or individually. In auto-resize mode the engine keeps these aligned to the canvas.
members.depthTest: When `false`, the camera ignores the depth buffer entirely — no depth test, no depth write — and composites every renderable in submission order, like a 2D canvas: what is drawn later appears on top, regardless of its distance. Distance sorting is skipped as well, so transparentSort has no effect.
members.elevatePosition: Moves the camera position up or down along a sphere centered at target. Useful for orbit elevation.
members.elevateView: Tilts the camera's look direction up or down (pitch) by `angle` degrees. Position stays fixed.
members.farClip: Near and far clip plane distances. Objects closer than `nearClip` or further than `farClip` are not rendered. Tighten these bounds to maximise depth-buffer precision.
members.getDistanceFromTarget: Returns the distance between the camera position and the current target point. Useful for zoom limits in orbit controllers.
members.getProjectionMatrix: Computed matrices ready to pass to shaders or custom render pipelines.
members.getViewMatrix: Computed matrices ready to pass to shaders or custom render pipelines.
members.getViewProjectionMatrix: Computed matrices ready to pass to shaders or custom render pipelines.
members.leftClip: Orthographic frustum extents. Set via setOrtho or individually. In auto-resize mode the engine keeps these aligned to the canvas.
members.nearClip: Near and far clip plane distances. Objects closer than `nearClip` or further than `farClip` are not rendered. Tighten these bounds to maximise depth-buffer precision.
members.renderToTexture: When `true`, the camera renders to an internal Framebuffer instead of the main window surface. Retrieve the framebuffer with `getFramebuffer()` and pass it to a `Mesh::setTexture` call to create render-to-texture effects.
members.rightClip: Orthographic frustum extents. Set via setOrtho or individually. In auto-resize mode the engine keeps these aligned to the canvas.
members.rotatePosition: Orbits the camera's position around the current target by `angle` degrees. Useful for orbit camera controllers.
members.rotateView: Rotates the camera's look direction around the up axis by `angle` degrees (yaw). The camera position stays fixed.
members.screenToRay: Converts a screen-space position (in canvas pixels) to a world-space Ray for mouse picking.
members.setOrtho: Configures the camera for orthographic projection with explicit clip planes. All objects within the box `(left, right, bottom, top, near, far)` are rendered.
members.setPerspective: Configures the camera for perspective (3D) projection.
members.target: Look-at point in local space. When set, the camera orientation is computed each frame so the camera always faces this point. Disable with disableTarget.
members.topClip: Orthographic frustum extents. Set via setOrtho or individually. In auto-resize mode the engine keeps these aligned to the canvas.
members.transparentSort: Enables back-to-front depth sorting for transparent objects from this camera's viewpoint. Disable for orthographic UI cameras where order is determined by hierarchy. It only applies while depthTest is on — without a depth buffer the camera already draws in submission order.
members.type: Switches between orthographic and perspective projection. Setting the type does not automatically recalculate clip planes; use setOrtho or setPerspective for that.
members.up: Local up vector used when computing the view matrix from a target. Defaults to `(0, 1, 0)`.
members.updateCamera: Forces an immediate recalculation of view and projection matrices. Called automatically each frame; call manually only when you need a fresh matrix outside the normal update cycle.
members.walkForward: Moves the camera forward along its look direction by `distance` units.
members.yfov: Vertical field-of-view in degrees (when `Engine::useDegrees` is `true`). Affects how wide the perspective frustum opens.
members.zoom: Moves the camera position along the direction toward target by `distance` units. A positive value zooms in; negative zooms out.

Character3D.description: `Character3D` moves a 3D character over the physics world: it walks along the ground, climbs steps, walks up ramps that are not too steep, slides down the ones that are, keeps to the ground going down, rides moving platforms, pushes dynamic bodies and falls with gravity. It is built on Jolt Physics' CharacterVirtual, so it is not a rigid body: it never tips over, never bounces and never slides on its own when it stands still.

members.airControl: How much the character steers in the air, from `0` to `1`. `1` moves it in the air as on the ground. `0` keeps the horizontal velocity it had when it left the ground, so a jump follows its arc whatever the input. Values in between steer from that velocity towards moveVelocity at every fixed step.
members.gravityFactor: Scales the scene's 3D gravity for this character. `0` makes it fly where moveVelocity and linearVelocity take it.
members.jump: At the next fixed step the character leaves with this upward speed, added to the velocity of the ground it stands on. It does not check the ground itself: call it when isOnGround is true, or count jumps for a double jump. A ceiling stops the rise at once.
members.linearVelocity: The velocity the last step moved the character with, gravity, jumps and the ground's velocity included. Walls and the ground stop the character without changing it: standing, it reads a small downward speed, and against a wall the full walking speed. Use the ground state to tell standing from falling.
members.load: Rebuilds the character from its Character3DComponent. Call it after changing a component value that only applies when the character is built: `height`, `radius`, `padding` or `innerBody`. The physics system builds the character on its own when the scene loads, and the methods that read the character build it when a script's `init` runs first. Setting position or calling setShape before then only sets where and how it will be built. A character that cannot be built, such as one scaled to zero, is tried again when its scale changes.
members.mass: `mass` (kg) is the weight the character puts on dynamic bodies it stands on. `maxStrength` (N) is the force it pushes dynamic bodies with when it walks into them: a body heavier than that force can move against its friction stays where it is.
members.maxSlopeAngle: The steepest ground, in degrees, that the character walks on. Steeper ground reports `ON_STEEP_GROUND`: the character slides down it and walking into it does not climb it.
members.maxStrength: `mass` (kg) is the weight the character puts on dynamic bodies it stands on. `maxStrength` (N) is the force it pushes dynamic bodies with when it walks into them: a body heavier than that force can move against its friction stays where it is.
members.moveVelocity: The velocity the character walks with, in world units per second. Only its horizontal part is used, so a direction from the camera can be passed as it is. It is kept until changed: set it every frame from input, and set it to zero to stop. Below 1 cm/s the character counts as standing still, so input eased toward zero does not leave it creeping down a slope it can walk.
members.position: The feet of the character, in world space. Setting it teleports the character and the entity's transform at once and finds its contacts again, so `isOnGround` is right before the next step. Called from a physics callback, such as a sensor's `onContactAdded3D`, the teleport waits for the next step.
members.setShape: Changes the capsule while the character keeps playing, for example to crouch. It returns `false` and keeps the old capsule when the new one would not fit where the character stands, so a crouching character cannot stand up under a low ceiling. Like the component values, the sizes are scaled by the entity's scale. It cannot be called from a physics callback. On a character that is not built yet, it sets the size it will be built with and returns `true`.
members.stepDown: `stepUp` is the highest step, in world units, that the character climbs while walking. The rounded bottom of the capsule rides over a low edge by itself, up to about `radius * (1 - cos(maxSlopeAngle))` (0.09 m for the default capsule), and that height adds to `stepUp` on a sharp edge. `0` leaves only what the rounded bottom climbs.
members.stepUp: `stepUp` is the highest step, in world units, that the character climbs while walking. The rounded bottom of the capsule rides over a low edge by itself, up to about `radius * (1 - cos(maxSlopeAngle))` (0.09 m for the default capsule), and that height adds to `stepUp` on a sharp edge. `0` leaves only what the rounded bottom climbs.

Collider3D.description: `Collider3D` is what an entity is in the 3D physics world: a Body3D or a Character3D. It is the base class of both, and the type of the two sides of the 3D contact events and of `shouldCollide3D`, so one handler serves bodies and characters: ask the side what it is, then use its own handle.

members.getAttachedObject: Returns the Object that owns the body or the character.
members.getBody3D: The handle of the same entity as a body or as a character. Unlike Object, neither adds a component, so check isBody3D or isCharacter3D first: the methods of a handle whose component is missing fail.
members.getCharacter3D: The handle of the same entity as a body or as a character. Unlike Object, neither adds a component, so check isBody3D or isCharacter3D first: the methods of a handle whose component is missing fail.
members.isBody3D: Which one the entity is. An entity with both components is a body, so at most one of them is `true`; both are `false` for an entity with neither.
members.isCharacter3D: Which one the entity is. An entity with both components is a body, so at most one of them is `true`; both are `false` for an entity with neither.
members.linearVelocity: How fast the body or the character moves, in meters per second, as its own `linearVelocity` reads it. It is read-only here.
members.position: Where the body or the character is in the world, as its own `position` reads it. It is read-only here: move it through getBody3D or getCharacter3D.

Color.description: A static utility class providing colour space conversion between linear (physically-based) and sRGB (perceptually uniform, display-encoded) colour spaces.

members.linearTosRGB: Converts a linear colour to sRGB display-encoded space. Use this when you need to display a physically-accurate linear value to the user as a readable colour (e.g. in a UI colour picker).
members.sRGBToLinear: Converts an sRGB colour to linear space. Use this before assigning a colour from a design tool or a hex code to a Material or light property.

ColorAction.description: Animates the `color` property of its target object, interpolating from a start colour to an end colour over a fixed duration. Both RGB (`Vector3`) and RGBA (`Vector4`) variants are available.

members.setAction: Configures the tween. The `Vector3` overload interpolates RGB; the `Vector4` overload includes alpha. `duration` is in seconds.

Container.description: An invisible layout container that automatically arranges child UI elements in a vertical or horizontal stack, with optional wrapping. Add UI children as child entities of the container's Object; the container measures and positions them each frame.

members.getContentHeight: Returns the total size of all laid-out children. Use this to size a Scrollbar relative to the visible area.
members.getContentWidth: Returns the total size of all laid-out children. Use this to size a Scrollbar relative to the visible area.
members.resize: Forces an immediate layout recalculation. Normally the container updates automatically each frame, but you can call this after batch-adding children to avoid a one-frame lag.
members.setBoxExpand: Controls whether a specific child slot expands to fill available space. When `expand` is `true`, the slot grows to fill the remaining parent area not occupied by fixed-size children.
members.useAllWrapSpace: When `true` and the layout is a wrap type, the cells are distributed evenly to fill the available space.
members.wrapCellHeight: Fixed cell size used when the layout type is `VERTICAL_WRAP` or `HORIZONTAL_WRAP`.
members.wrapCellWidth: Fixed cell size used when the layout type is `VERTICAL_WRAP` or `HORIZONTAL_WRAP`.

Data.description: An in-memory byte buffer that implements the `FileData` streaming interface. It can be loaded from a file path, from a raw byte pointer, or from another File object. Once loaded, it supports sequential read/write operations and random seek access.

members.eof: Returns non-zero (`true` in Lua) if the read cursor is at or past the end of the buffer.
members.length: Returns the total size of the buffer in bytes.
members.open: Loads data from a raw byte pointer, a file path, or a File object. The filename overload transparently reads packed `asset://`, `lua://`, and asset-relative paths in a native export. When `aCopy` is `true`, the data is duplicated into an internal buffer; when `aTakeOwnership` is `true`, the `Data` object takes ownership of the provided pointer. The `File` overload reads from the file's current position, and returns `FileErrors::INVALID_PARAMETER` when the file is not open. Lua has the filename overload only.
members.read: Read or write `aBytes` bytes at the current cursor position. Returns the number of bytes actually transferred.
members.seek: Moves the read/write cursor to `aOffset` bytes from the beginning. A negative offset counts back from the end, and the cursor always stays between the start and the end of the data.
members.write: Read or write `aBytes` bytes at the current cursor position. Returns the number of bytes actually transferred.

Engine.description: Control engine properties and define defaults used across the whole project. `Engine` is entirely static — never instantiated. It manages the scene stack, canvas size and scaling, the update loop, platform queries, and all frame/input callback events.

members.addSceneLayer: Renders an additional scene as a layer on top of the main scene. Commonly used for HUDs, overlays, or pause menus.
members.allowEventsOutCanvas: When `true`, mouse move and scroll events are delivered even when the cursor is outside the canvas bounds.
members.asyncLoading: Enable background resource loading. When active, GPU resource creation must be committed on the main thread via commitThreadQueue.
members.callMouseInTouchEvent: When `true`, receiving a touch event also fires the equivalent mouse event. Useful for cross-platform testing.
members.callTouchInMouseEvent: When `true`, receiving a mouse event also fires the equivalent touch event.
members.canvasHeight: Logical canvas dimensions after scaling is applied. These may differ from preferredCanvasWidth when a non-NATIVE scaling mode is active.
members.canvasWidth: Logical canvas dimensions after scaling is applied. These may differ from preferredCanvasWidth when a non-NATIVE scaling mode is active.
members.clearAllSubscriptions: Removes all registered callbacks from all engine events. When `includeLifecycle` is `false`, lifecycle events such as `onViewLoaded` are preserved.
members.clearComponentSubscriptions: Removes the callbacks registered on a scene's components — Button `onPress`, UI pointer and focus events, panel, scrollbar, text edit, sound, and action events. clearAllSubscriptions covers the engine's own events; this one covers the per-component events.
members.clearPools: Fully clears the texture, texture-data, model, shader, sound, and font caches. This also destroys pooled GPU textures and shaders, including entries that are still referenced elsewhere. Use it for engine or graphics-view teardown, not routine level unloading.
members.clearUnusedPools: Removes cache entries that are no longer referenced outside their pool while keeping resources that active scenes or engine objects still own. Pending sound and decoded texture-data work is allowed to finish before those caches are swept. Shader missing/failed state and custom-shader registrations are also reset.
members.commitThreadQueue: Used to safely create GPU resources from background threads:
members.deltatime: Time elapsed in seconds since the last draw frame. Multiply movement speeds by `deltatime` inside `onUpdate` to make motion frame-rate independent.
members.endAsyncThread: Used to safely create GPU resources from background threads:
members.executeSceneOnce: Adds a scene that runs for a single draw, then is automatically removed. Useful for rendering a scene to a texture on demand, such as a thumbnail or a preview image. Passing `nullptr` has no effect.
members.frameStats: Draw counters for the last completed `systemDraw`: GPU submissions, not CPU work. C++ only — Lua can read framerate but not these fields.
members.framebuffer: Off-screen render target for the full frame output. When set, the engine renders to this framebuffer instead of the window surface.
members.framerate: Current frames-per-second estimate. Computed from the raw (unclamped) frame time, so it stays accurate even on stalled frames where deltatime is clamped.
members.getLastScene: Returns the top-most scene in the stack (the most recently added layer, or the main scene if no layers exist).
members.getMainScene: Returns the scene set with setScene.
members.getQueuedResourceCount: Returns the number of resources still waiting to be loaded on background threads.
members.getScene: Returns the current main scene, or `nullptr`/`nil` if none is set.
members.getViewRect: Returns the viewport rectangle calculated from canvas size, window size, and scaling mode.
members.hasScenesToExecuteOnce: Returns `true` while any scene queued with executeSceneOnce is still waiting to be drawn. Useful when the draw loop only runs on demand: a renderer that skips idle frames must keep drawing while this is `true`, or the queued scenes never render.
members.ignoreEventsHandledByUI: When `true`, gameplay input callbacks are skipped for events already consumed by a UI widget. That covers pointer and touch events, and the keys, gamepad buttons, and left stick that move and press the focused button.
members.interpolationAlpha: Value in `0, 1)` representing how far the current rendered frame is between the previous and next fixed-update steps. Physics bodies are already drawn with it (see [PhysicsSystem interpolation); use it to interpolate anything else you move from `onFixedUpdate`.
members.isAsyncThread: Used to safely create GPU resources from background threads:
members.isSceneRunning: Returns `true` if the given scene is currently in the active scene stack.
members.isUIEventReceived: Returns `true` inside an input callback when a UI widget consumed that event. With ignoreEventsHandledByUI turned off, gameplay code can use it to skip UI clicks and menu keys.
members.isViewLoaded: Returns `true` after the graphics surface is ready (after onViewLoaded fires).
members.maxDeltatime: Upper bound, in seconds, for the value returned by deltatime and used by the update loop. Lower it for stricter clamping; raise it to allow larger single steps. Must be greater than `0`. Equivalent to Unity's `Time.maximumDeltaTime`.
members.mouseCursor: Changes the OS mouse cursor shape. See CursorType.
members.mouseMode: Sets how the mouse cursor behaves — a single state that covers both its visibility and whether it is free, locked, or confined. See MouseMode for every value.
members.onCanvasChanged: Called when the canvas or window size changes. Re-query canvasWidth/canvasHeight or reposition UI elements here.
members.onCharInput: Called for text input. Prefer this over onKeyDown when implementing text fields.
members.onDraw: Called every frame after the updates, right before the scenes are drawn. A minimized Windows, Linux, or macOS game keeps updating without drawing and skips it, as does a macOS game whose window can't be seen, so keep game logic in onUpdate.
members.onFixedUpdate: Called at a fixed interval defined by updateTime. Use for physics, deterministic simulation, and anything that must not depend on frame rate.
members.onGamepadAxisMove: Called when an analog axis (stick or trigger) changes. For always-on movement, polling Input.getGamepadAxis in `onUpdate` is usually simpler than tracking this event.
members.onGamepadButtonDown: Called when a controller button is pressed.
members.onGamepadButtonUp: Called when a controller button is released.
members.onGamepadConnect: Called when a controller is connected (and once for each controller already connected at startup). Query its name with Input.getGamepadName.
members.onGamepadDisconnect: Called when a controller is disconnected. After this fires, Input.isGamepadConnected returns `false` for that id.
members.onKeyDown: Called when any keyboard key is pressed.
members.onKeyUp: Called when any keyboard key is released.
members.onMouseDown: Called when a mouse button is pressed.
members.onMouseEnter: Called when the mouse cursor enters the canvas boundary.
members.onMouseLeave: Called when the mouse cursor leaves the canvas boundary.
members.onMouseMove: Called when the mouse cursor moves. Also called outside the canvas when allowEventsOutCanvas is `true`.
members.onMouseScroll: Called when the mouse scroll wheel changes.
members.onMouseUp: Called when a mouse button is released.
members.onPause: Called when the system suspends the application (e.g. phone call received, app moved to background). It also fires while a full-screen ad covers the game and while a web portal pauses it; see Ads pause the game.
members.onPostUpdate: Called after the regular update and fixed-update passes each frame. Useful for late-stage logic such as camera follow that must run after all objects have moved.
members.onResume: Called when the application returns to the foreground after a pause, including after each full-screen ad.
members.onSceneLoaded: Called once a scene stack loaded by `SceneManager::loadScene` has loaded its resources, and once for the start scene, both in exported games and in the editor's Play. It fires before the loading scene closes, so a level can place its player and camera behind it. `SceneManager::isLoading()` is still `true` here, and a loading scene can hold the load to fade out. `addChildScene` does not fire it.
members.onShutdown: Called when the application is closing. Use to flush saves or clean up persistent state.
members.onTouchCancel: Called when a tracked touch is interrupted, after it has been removed from `Input`. A per-pointer cancellation preserves other active touches. A full cancellation removes all tracked touches before emitting this callback once per touch. There is no separate global callback, and a full cancellation with no tracked touches emits nothing. Canceling an unknown or already removed identifier also emits nothing. Use `Input::numTouches()` (`Input.numTouches()` in Lua) to check whether any fingers remain; it is zero during every full-cancel callback.
members.onTouchEnd: Called when a touch contact is lifted.
members.onTouchMove: Called whenever a touch contact moves.
members.onTouchStart: Called when a new touch contact begins.
members.onUpdate: Called every frame for variable-step gameplay logic. Multiply movement by deltatime to ensure frame-rate independence.
members.onViewDestroyed: Called when the graphics surface is being destroyed (e.g. app going to background on mobile).
members.onViewLoaded: Called once when the graphics backend surface is ready for rendering.
members.openGL: Returns `true` when any OpenGL backend (GLCORE, GLES3) is active.
members.pauseGameEvents: Pauses delivery of gameplay events (onUpdate, onFixedUpdate, input callbacks) without stopping the render loop. The editor uses this when the project is not in play mode.
members.platform: Returns the Platform the engine is currently running on.
members.preferredCanvasHeight: The dimensions originally passed to setCanvasSize, unaffected by scaling.
members.preferredCanvasWidth: The dimensions originally passed to setCanvasSize, unaffected by scaling.
members.removeAllSceneLayers: Removes all layered scenes. When `removeOneTimeScenes` is `true`, one-time scenes added via executeSceneOnce are also removed.
members.removeAllScenes: Removes all scenes, including the main scene and all layers.
members.removeScene: Removes a specific scene from the active scene stack. If it was queued with executeSceneOnce, the pending one-shot execution is cancelled so the scene can be destroyed safely after this method returns.
members.scalingMode: Controls how the logical canvas is mapped to the physical window. See Scaling for each mode. Like setCanvasSize, a change applies immediately to the running scenes.
members.setCanvasSize: Sets the preferred logical canvas dimensions. The actual canvasWidth/canvasHeight reported at runtime may differ depending on the active scalingMode. It applies immediately, also while a scene runs: UI and auto-resized cameras follow the new size.
members.setMaxResourceLoadingThreads: Sets the maximum number of worker threads used for background asset loading.
members.setMousePosition: Sets the mouse position in logical canvas coordinates and updates `Input.getMousePosition()`.
members.setScene: Sets the main scene. Pass `nullptr` (C++) or `nil` (Lua) to clear the main scene.
members.setUpdateTimeMS: Same as updateTime but accepts the interval in milliseconds.
members.startAsyncThread: Used to safely create GPU resources from background threads:
members.systemTime: Monotonic wall-clock time in seconds, independent of scene pausing and update loop throttling.
members.textureStrategy: Controls automatic resizing of non-power-of-two textures on hardware that requires it. It applies to textures loaded after it is set.
members.updateTime: Fixed-update interval in seconds. Used by `onFixedUpdate` and the physics simulation step. Also accepted in milliseconds via setUpdateTimeMS.
members.useDegrees: When `true` (default), angle parameters in the API expect degrees. Set to `false` to use radians throughout.
members.viewRect: Viewport rectangle computed from canvas size, screen size, and scaling mode.

EntityHandle.description: The base class for all high-level Doriax objects that wrap an ECS entity. `EntityHandle` stores a reference to its owning `Scene` and its `Entity` identifier, giving C++ and Lua code a convenient handle to a scene entity without having to interact with the raw ECS API.

members.entityOwned: Whether this handle owns its entity. When `true`, the entity is destroyed (and any sub-resources it set up are cleared) when the handle is destroyed. Set it to `false` to detach the handle from the entity's lifetime.
members.getEntity: Returns the raw ECS entity identifier. Use this when interfacing with the low-level EntityManager or EntityRegistry APIs.
members.getScene: Returns a pointer to the owning Scene.
members.name: Human-readable tag for this entity. Used by the editor to display entities in the scene hierarchy, and can be used in game code for debugging or lookup.

Fog.description: Applies atmospheric fog to a scene. Fog blends the scene's rendered colour towards a fog colour based on the depth of each fragment from the camera, simulating haze, mist, or distance-based visibility falloff.

members.color: The fog colour in linear space. Match this to your sky colour for a natural-looking effect.
members.density: The density coefficient for `EXPONENTIAL` and `EXPONENTIALSQUARED` modes. Larger values produce thicker fog.
members.linearEnd: The near and far clip distances for `LINEAR` fog. Objects closer than `linearStart` are unaffected; objects beyond `linearEnd` are fully in the fog colour.
members.linearStart: The near and far clip distances for `LINEAR` fog. Objects closer than `linearStart` are unaffected; objects beyond `linearEnd` are fully in the fog colour.

Image.description: The foundational 2D UI visual element. `Image` renders a textured or colour-filled rectangle with optional 9-patch scaling. It is the base class for Button, Panel, Progressbar, Scrollbar, and TextEdit.

members.color: The tint colour multiplied with the texture, in sRGB. `(1,1,1,1)` renders the texture as-is. Changing the colour is a cheap way to create hover/pressed states without separate textures.
members.createImage: Explicitly builds the image geometry and GPU buffers. This method is C++ only and is normally optional because the UI system builds and rebuilds images automatically. Use it when C++ code needs the geometry immediately.
members.flipY: Flips the texture vertically. Useful when a texture is loaded upside-down or for certain rendering passes.
members.getAABB: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box in local or world space. Useful for hit-testing or layout calculations.
members.getWorldAABB: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box in local or world space. Useful for hit-testing or layout calculations.
members.onClick: Called on a complete click (press + release inside the element) or double click.
members.onDoubleClick: Called on a complete click (press + release inside the element) or double click.
members.onDrag: Fired when the user begins dragging, continues dragging, or releases while dragging this element.
members.onDragEnd: Fired when the user begins dragging, continues dragging, or releases while dragging this element.
members.onDragStart: Fired when the user begins dragging, continues dragging, or releases while dragging this element.
members.onGetFocus: Called when this element gains or loses keyboard focus.
members.onLostFocus: Called when this element gains or loses keyboard focus.
members.onPointerDown: Called on mouse/touch press and release.
members.onPointerEnter: Called when the mouse pointer enters or leaves the element boundary.
members.onPointerLeave: Called when the mouse pointer enters or leaves the element boundary.
members.onPointerMove: Called each frame the pointer moves while over this element.
members.onPointerUp: Called on mouse/touch press and release.
members.patchMargin: Sets the 9-patch insets. When all four margins are zero (the default), the image is scaled uniformly. Setting the margins enables 9-patch mode where the corners are preserved.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without reloading the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.setTexture: Assigns the texture to display. Pass a file path, in-memory pixel data with a cache id, or a framebuffer for render-to-texture UI.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `ui` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the image draws with, such as `"shaders/glow.glsl"`. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultUIShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. It is the `shader` field of UIComponent; see Custom Shaders.
members.textureScaleFactor: Insets the UV rectangle by this many texels on every side, `0.0` by default. A small value such as `0.5` pulls the sampled area away from the edges of a packed atlas cell, hiding the neighbouring pixels that bilinear filtering would otherwise bleed in.

InAppPurchase.description: One-time products, consumable or not, and subscriptions, through Google Play Billing on Android and StoreKit 2 on iOS. Exports include it only when Google Play Billing is enabled in the project's Android settings, or App Store Purchases in its iOS settings. On every other platform the calls report `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` through their events.

members.acknowledgePurchase: Settle a `PURCHASED` purchase. Google Play refunds one left unsettled for three days, and the App Store delivers it again at every launch. On iOS, settling finishes the purchase's transactions.
members.changeSubscription: Replaces an owned subscription with another plan or product, an upgrade or a downgrade. `oldPurchaseToken` must belong to a purchase in `getPurchases()`, so query `SUBS` purchases first; otherwise `onPurchaseFailed` reports `DEVELOPER_ERROR`. `mode` decides how the time left on the old plan is billed. `KEEP_EXISTING` keeps the old plan's payment schedule and ignores `offerToken`.
members.getProduct: The products queried so far. `getProduct()` returns an empty `ProductDetails` for a product that was not queried, so check `hasProduct()` first.
members.getPurchases: The purchases known in this session, from purchase screens and `queryPurchases`, less the consumed ones. `isPurchased()` is true when one of them includes the product, is `PURCHASED`, and is not `suspended`. It does not check acknowledgment.
members.hasProduct: The products queried so far. `getProduct()` returns an empty `ProductDetails` for a product that was not queried, so check `hasProduct()` first.
members.initialize: Connects to the store. `onInitialized(response, message)` reports `OK` once it is ready, and every call before that fails with `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED`. Calling `initialize()` again while connected reports `OK` again.
members.openSubscriptionManagement: Opens the store's subscription management, on one subscription or on all of them, where the player can cancel or fix a payment. On Android it opens Google Play's subscription center. On iOS it shows Apple's subscription sheet over the game, on the product's subscription group from iOS 17, and queries the subscriptions again when it closes.
members.purchase: Opens the store's purchase screen for a queried product. The result is `onPurchaseUpdated` for a completed or pending purchase, or `onPurchaseFailed(productId, response, message)`, for example with `USER_CANCELED`, `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED`, or `ITEM_UNAVAILABLE` for a product that was not queried.
members.queryProducts: Fetches the details of these products, which must all be of `type`: their localized names, descriptions, prices and, for subscriptions, plans and offers. `onProductsQueried(response, message)` reports when they are stored, and products the store does not know are left out. On iOS so are products of the other type, and the message names both kinds. An empty list reports `DEVELOPER_ERROR`. In Lua, pass a table of strings.
members.queryPurchases: Asks the store for the player's purchases of `type`: active subscriptions, products bought once, and consumables not consumed yet. Each one is reported through `onPurchaseUpdated` with `restored` set, then `onPurchasesQueried(type, response, message)` fires. With `OK`, the result replaces the stored purchases of that type, so refunded and expired ones go away.
members.restorePurchases: For a Restore Purchases button: queries the purchases of both types, as two `queryPurchases` calls do. On iOS it first syncs the player's App Store account, which may ask them to sign in; a failed sync reports its error through both `onPurchasesQueried` events. Apple's review guidelines ask apps to offer a way to restore purchases that can be restored.
members.setObfuscatedAccountId: A hashed id of the player's account in your game, and of a profile within it, attached to the next purchases. Google Play uses them against fraud, and they come back in `PurchaseDetails` for your server. Never pass plain personal data.
members.showInAppMessages: Lets Google Play show its messages about subscription payment problems, such as a declined card. When the player fixes the payment, subscription purchases are queried again, and `onPurchaseUpdated` reports the subscription without `suspended`. It does nothing on iOS, which shows these messages by itself.

Input.description: `Input` is a static polling class that provides the current keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad state at any point during a frame. Use it inside `onUpdate` or `onFixedUpdate` to check whether a key or button is held down. For event-based input (press/release and controller connect/disconnect notifications), subscribe to the Engine callback events instead.

members.findGamepadIndex: Returns the internal index of the controller with the given id, or `SIZE_MAX` if it is not connected. Most code should use isGamepadConnected and getGamepadId instead.
members.findTouchIndex: Returns the index into the getTouches array for the given pointer ID. Returns `SIZE_MAX` if not found.
members.getGamepadAxis: Returns the current value of an analog axis on controller `id`, in the range `-1.0`…`1.0`. Use `D_GAMEPAD_AXIS_*` constants in C++ and `Input.GAMEPAD_AXIS_*` in Lua. Returns `0.0` for an unknown controller.
members.getGamepadId: Returns the real id of the `index`-th connected controller, or `-1` if `index` is out of range. Because gamepad ids are sparse (they can have gaps after a disconnect), this is the correct way to enumerate connected controllers:
members.getGamepadName: Returns the human-readable name of the controller with the given id, or an empty string if it is not connected.
members.getGamepads: Returns all connected controllers. Each `Gamepad` holds an `int id`, a `std::string name`, and the current button and axis state. In Lua, iterate with numGamepads and getGamepadId instead.
members.getModifiers: Returns the current modifier key bitmask. Check individual modifiers with bitwise AND.
members.getMousePosition: Current cursor position in canvas coordinates. Updated every frame; use for hover detection in `onUpdate`.
members.getMouseScroll: Accumulated scroll wheel delta since the last frame, in `(xoffset, yoffset)`. Reset each frame.
members.getTouchPosition: Returns the current position of the touch contact identified by `pointer`. Use findTouchIndex to convert a pointer ID to an array index if needed.
members.getTouches: Returns all active touch contacts. Each `Touch` has `int pointer` and `Vector2 position`.
members.isGamepadButtonPressed: Returns `true` while the given button is held down on controller `id`. Use `D_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` constants in C++ and `Input.GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` in Lua. Returns `false` for an unknown controller.
members.isGamepadConnected: Returns `true` while a controller with the given id is connected. Ids are assigned per platform and are sparse — enumerate connected controllers with getGamepadId, not by assuming ids `0..numGamepads()-1`.
members.isKeyPressed: Returns `true` while the given key is held down. Use `D_KEY_*` constants in C++ and `Input.KEY_*` in Lua for the key code.
members.isMouseEntered: Returns `true` while the mouse cursor is inside the canvas boundary.
members.isMousePressed: Returns `true` while the given mouse button is held down. Use `D_MOUSE_BUTTON_*` constants in C++ and `Input.MOUSE_BUTTON_*` in Lua.
members.isTouch: Returns `true` if there is at least one active touch contact.
members.numGamepads: Returns the count of currently connected controllers. This is a count, not the highest id — combine it with getGamepadId to iterate.
members.numTouches: Returns the count of currently active touch contacts.

members.setDistanceJoint: Keeps two bodies at the distance their anchors have when the joint is created. The first form anchors at each body's position, the second takes anchors in world space. With `rope` set to `true` the joint acts like a rope: the bodies can move closer, but never farther apart than that distance. This is the Rope option of a Distance joint in the editor.
members.setMouseJoint: Grabs the dynamic `bodyA` at `target`, in world space, and holds that point there with a soft spring, so the body hangs from it and swings to rest. The target stays fixed in the world: `bodyB` must be another body but takes no force and doesn't carry the target, and `bodyA` still collides with it. Removing or disabling `bodyB` releases `bodyA`, and the joint comes back when `bodyB` does.

KeyframeTracks.description: Base class of the keyframe track actions: TranslateTracks, RotateTracks, ScaleTracks and MorphTracks. It holds what they share: the key times, the per-segment easing, looping and relative values. Each subclass adds `setValues` with one value per key.

members.loop: When `true`, the track starts over after its last key instead of stopping, so a track loops on its own without an Animation.
members.relative: When `true`, the values are offsets from the pose the target has when the track starts: a translation adds to its position, a rotation is applied after its rotation and a scale multiplies its scale. The track then works wherever the target is placed. A UI element with anchors moves by its layout offset. Morph tracks ignore it. See Relative tracks.
