members.setEasing: `setEasing(segment, ease)` sets the easing of a single segment (key `segment` to key `segment + 1`); `setEasings(list)` replaces the whole per-segment list. Missing entries mean linear, `STEP` holds each key's value until the next key, and `CUSTOM` is not storable per segment (treated as linear). See Per-segment easing.
members.setEasings: `setEasing(segment, ease)` sets the easing of a single segment (key `segment` to key `segment + 1`); `setEasings(list)` replaces the whole per-segment list. Missing entries mean linear, `STEP` holds each key's value until the next key, and `CUSTOM` is not storable per segment (treated as linear). See Per-segment easing.
members.setTimes: Sets the key times in seconds, in ascending order. Trims the easing list when the key count shrinks.

Light.description: Represents a light source in a 3D scene. Doriax supports three light types — directional, point, and spot — all sharing the same `Light` class. The light type determines which properties have effect: a directional light uses `direction` and an unlimited `range`, a point light radiates in all directions with a finite `range`, and a spot light uses `direction` with either cone angles or an optional projected mask.

members.automaticShadowCamera: When `true`, the engine automatically fits the shadow-map camera frustum around the visible scene each frame, optimising shadow quality. Disable this if you need manual control over cameraNear / cameraFar.
members.bias: The shadow-map depth bias added to prevent self-shadowing artefacts (shadow acne). Increase this value if you see acne on surfaces; decrease it if you see shadows detaching from geometry (Peter-panning). A good starting value is `0.005`.
members.cameraFar: The near and far clip planes of the shadow-map camera. Tighten these around the scene geometry to maximise shadow-map precision. `setShadowCameraNearFar()` sets both at once.
members.cameraNear: The near and far clip planes of the shadow-map camera. Tighten these around the scene geometry to maximise shadow-map precision. `setShadowCameraNearFar()` sets both at once.
members.cascadeBlend: Fades each cascade into the next over a short band past its split, which hides the line where the shadow resolution changes. Only relevant for `DIRECTIONAL` lights with more than one cascade. It is off by default because the band samples two cascades and the finer one draws more casters.
members.color: The RGB color of the emitted light, in sRGB. Each channel ranges from `0.0` to `1.0` for standard colours, though values above `1.0` are valid for HDR scenes. It is stored linear internally, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one.
members.direction: The normalised direction vector the light shines towards. Used by `DIRECTIONAL` and `SPOT` lights.
members.innerConeAngle: Define the shape of a `SPOT` light. The angle is specified in degrees (or radians if `Engine::useDegrees` is `false`).
members.intensity: A multiplier applied to the light's color. `1.0` is the default. Higher values create a brighter light without altering the hue. At `0` the light is off and leaves its slot to another light.
members.numCascades: Number of cascades for Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM). Only relevant for `DIRECTIONAL` lights. More cascades distribute shadow-map resolution more evenly across the view frustum, reducing the "blurry distant shadows" artefact at the cost of additional render passes. Typical values are `1` (off) to `4`.
members.outerConeAngle: Define the shape of a `SPOT` light. The angle is specified in degrees (or radians if `Engine::useDegrees` is `false`).
members.range: The maximum distance (in world units) at which the light has any effect. Relevant for `POINT` and `SPOT` lights. `DIRECTIONAL` lights have an infinite range and ignore this value.
members.shadowMapSize: The resolution of the shadow map texture in pixels (e.g. `512`, `1024`, `2048`). Higher values produce sharper shadows at the cost of GPU memory and fillrate. Must be a power of two.
members.shadows: Enables shadow map generation for this light. Shadow casting also requires the caster mesh to have `castShadows` enabled and the receiver mesh to have `receiveShadows` enabled. See the Mesh documentation.
members.spotMask: An optional image projected by a `SPOT` light. It replaces the default circular cone attenuation, allowing shapes such as windows, logos, arrows, and soft-edged patterns without a separate spot-shape setting. The `spotMask` property only reads the current mask in either language; `setSpotMask` and `clearSpotMask` are the write path, Lua included.
members.type: The light model to use. See LightType for the available values. Changing the type at run-time is supported.

Light2D.description: A point light for 2D scenes. Unlike Light, which drives the 3D PBR pipeline, a `Light2D` lives in the scene's XY plane and uses a simple radius falloff designed for the classic 2D look. Light from every `Light2D` is added on top of the scene's 2D ambient light (see Scene — setAmbientLight2D); dim the ambient to make lights visible.

members.color: The RGB color of the emitted light, in sRGB. Each channel ranges from `0.0` to `1.0`. It is stored linear internally, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one.
members.falloff: The attenuation exponent. Brightness fades as `pow(1 - distance/range, falloff)`: `1.0` is a linear fade, higher values concentrate the light near its center, values below `1.0` push light towards the edge of the range.
members.height: A virtual Z height of the light above the 2D plane. With a height greater than zero, the light has a direction relative to each surface point, so normal maps on sprites produce relief shading that shifts as the light moves. With `0.0` (default) the light is purely radial and normals are ignored.
members.intensity: A multiplier applied to the light's color. `1.0` is the default. Higher values create a brighter light without altering the hue.
members.mapResolution: The width in pixels of this light's 1D polar shadow map. Higher values give more angular precision for distant or thin occluders. The shadow atlas is sized by the largest `mapResolution` among the shadow-casting lights.
members.range: The radius of the light in world units. Nothing beyond this distance receives any light. In the editor, the range is drawn as a circle around the selected light.
members.shadowBias: Depth bias for the shadow comparison, in normalized units of the light's range. Increase it if surfaces right at an occluder edge show shadow acne; decrease it if shadows detach from their occluders.
members.shadowSoftness: The penumbra half-width, in shadow-map texels. `0.0` gives hard edges; values around `2.0`–`4.0` give a soft natural edge. If a wide penumbra shows banding, raise the scene-wide filter quality — see Scene — shadow2DQuality.
members.shadows: Enables shadow casting for this light. Shadows are produced by Occluder2D components in the scene; the receiver mesh must have `receiveShadows` enabled. Each light's shadow darkens only that light's contribution — the scene's ambient light is never shadowed.

Lines.description: Renders a collection of 3D line segments. Useful for debug overlays, grids, trajectory paths, and other wireframe visuals. Each line is defined by two endpoints and an optional per-endpoint colour for gradient lines.

members.getLine: Returns a reference to the LineData at the given index. Modify in-place then call `updateLines()`.
members.getNumLines: Returns the current number of line segments.
members.load: Explicitly initialises the GPU buffer. This method is C++ only and is normally optional because the render system initialises lines automatically.
members.maxLines: Pre-allocates buffer space for this many lines. Resize before calling `load()` for best performance.
members.removeLine: Removes the line at `index`. All subsequent indices shift down.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. Changing it reloads the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `lines` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the lines draw with, such as `"shaders/laser.glsl"`. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultLinesShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. See Custom Shaders.
members.updateLine: Overwrites an existing line's endpoints and/or colour. Multiple overloads mirror `addLine()`. Call `updateLines()` afterwards.
members.updateLines: Uploads all pending line changes to the GPU. Must be called after any `addLine`, `updateLine`, or `removeLine` call.

Log.description: `Log` provides static methods for writing messages to the platform console or log sink. Output goes to the editor's Output panel during play mode, and to `stdout`/`logcat`/Xcode console on each platform. All methods accept `printf`-style format strings.

members.debug: Logs a `DEBUG`-level message. Use for state dumps, object creation, and lifecycle tracking during active development.
members.error: Logs an `ERROR`-level message. Use for critical failures that prevent correct execution.
members.print: Writes a plain message to the log with no severity prefix. Use for general informational output and debugging.
members.verbose: Logs a `VERBOSE`-level message. Typically compiled out in release; use for high-frequency trace output such as per-frame diagnostics.
members.warn: Logs a `WARN`-level message. Use for recoverable issues: missing optional resources, fallback paths taken, or unexpected but non-fatal conditions.

Material.description: A PBR (Physically Based Rendering) material definition that drives how a mesh surface looks under lighting. `Material` is a plain data struct — it holds colour factors, metallic/roughness values, up to five texture slots that correspond to the standard glTF 2.0 PBR workflow, and the shader the surface draws with.

members.alphaCutoff: `alphaMode` controls how the combined alpha from `baseColorFactor.a` and the base-colour texture is rendered:
members.alphaMode: `alphaMode` controls how the combined alpha from `baseColorFactor.a` and the base-colour texture is rendered:
members.baseColorFactor: The base linear-space RGBA colour multiplied with `baseColorTexture`. When no texture is assigned, this is the solid colour of the surface. How the combined alpha is interpreted depends on alphaMode.
members.baseColorTexture: A Texture that modulates the `baseColorFactor`. The texture's RGBA channels are multiplied component-wise with `baseColorFactor`. Supports 2D textures loaded from file or created from pixel data.
members.emissiveFactor: An additive linear-space RGB glow colour. The surface emits light of this colour independent of external lighting. Multiplied with `emissiveTexture` when present. Keep all channels at `0` (the default) to disable emission.
members.emissiveTexture: A Texture whose RGB channels are multiplied with `emissiveFactor` to produce surface emission. Useful for glowing screens, neon signs, or lava surfaces.
members.foliageTransmission: Light let through a thin surface when a light is behind it, `0`–`1` (values are clamped). Each light adds its intensity times the base colour, this factor, how directly the light shines through, and the same shadow term as direct lighting, so a leaf glows only where the sun actually reaches its back. `0` (the default) disables it; keep it there on opaque geometry. Unlit materials ignore it.
members.metallicRoughnessTexture: A Texture encoding metallic information in the blue channel and roughness in the green channel (following the glTF 2.0 specification). The red channel is unused.
members.name: An optional human-readable identifier for the material, usually set automatically when loading a Model from a GLTF file. Can be used to look up or display material information at runtime.
members.normalTexture: A tangent-space normal map Texture. Perturbs the surface normal per-pixel to simulate fine geometric detail without additional polygons.
members.occlusionTexture: A Texture used for baked ambient-occlusion. The red channel is sampled to darken areas that receive less indirect light (crevices, seams). Scale is fixed at `1.0`.
members.shader: `shader` is the project-relative path of the shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the submesh draws with. Empty uses the scene's defaultMeshShader, else the engine built-in. `shaderUniforms` holds the values of the shader's `#pragma param` parameters by name, and `shaderTextures` its texture parameters, which `setShaderTexture` and `getShaderTexture` set and read. Each submesh has its own material, so each can draw with its own shader and values.
members.shaderTextures: `shader` is the project-relative path of the shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the submesh draws with. Empty uses the scene's defaultMeshShader, else the engine built-in. `shaderUniforms` holds the values of the shader's `#pragma param` parameters by name, and `shaderTextures` its texture parameters, which `setShaderTexture` and `getShaderTexture` set and read. Each submesh has its own material, so each can draw with its own shader and values.
members.shaderUniforms: `shader` is the project-relative path of the shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the submesh draws with. Empty uses the scene's defaultMeshShader, else the engine built-in. `shaderUniforms` holds the values of the shader's `#pragma param` parameters by name, and `shaderTextures` its texture parameters, which `setShaderTexture` and `getShaderTexture` set and read. Each submesh has its own material, so each can draw with its own shader and values.

Mesh.description: `Mesh` is the base class for all renderable 3D objects. It exposes the material system (color, texture, PBR material, shader file), shadow casting and receiving, transparency control, face culling, automatic detail levels, and GPU instancing (including distance fade and per-view instance culling) for drawing thousands of objects in a single draw call.

members.addInstance: Appends a new instance with the specified transform, creating the instanced mesh if the entity does not have one yet. Growing past maxInstances doubles the capacity and reloads the mesh.
members.alpha: Shorthand for the alpha channel of color. Values below 1.0 require transparent to be enabled for correct rendering order.
members.autoTransparency: `transparent` marks the mesh for the transparent render pass (sorted back-to-front). `autoTransparency` detects blending from the material (`BLEND`, or `AUTO` when the texture or factor is translucent) and enables the transparent pass automatically. A blended submesh keeps depth testing but disables depth writes in the colour pass so overlapping translucent surfaces composite correctly.
members.castShadows: Shadow participation flags. Enabling both adds depth-map cost; disable on distant or small objects for performance.
members.clearInstances: Removes all instances from the instance list. The mesh geometry is preserved; call updateInstances afterwards.
members.color: Tint color multiplied with the material texture. `(1,1,1,1)` means no tint.
members.createInstancedMesh: Enables GPU instancing for this mesh. After calling this, use addInstance / updateInstance to populate the instance list, then updateInstances to flush changes to the GPU.
members.cullDistance: World-space distance from the main camera past which instances are dropped from the culled views (main camera and shadow slots). `0` (default) means unlimited; negative or non-finite values are ignored. A hard cut, unlike distanceFade: instances keep their size until they vanish, and it applies with custom shaders and SSR too, so hide it with fog. Requires cullInstances. Logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet.
members.cullInstances: When `true` (default), instances outside the main camera or a shadow atlas slot are left out of that view. Turn it off when a shader moves instances away from the bounds the CPU computed; the whole entity then skips frustum culling too. Logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet. See Culling granularity.
members.distanceFade: Instanced-mesh distance fade. When `distanceFade` is on, instances shrink toward their base between `fadeStart` and `fadeEnd`, both model-space distances from the camera. Toggling the flag reloads the mesh (shader variant `Ifd`); the two distances are uniforms and can change without a reload. `Fade End` must be greater than `Fade Start`. Logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet.
members.faceCulling: Enables or disables back-face culling globally for this mesh. Disable for double-sided geometry (e.g. leaves, cards): back faces are then lit with their normal flipped toward the viewer, as glTF double-sided materials are.
members.fadeEnd: Instanced-mesh distance fade. When `distanceFade` is on, instances shrink toward their base between `fadeStart` and `fadeEnd`, both model-space distances from the camera. Toggling the flag reloads the mesh (shader variant `Ifd`); the two distances are uniforms and can change without a reload. `Fade End` must be greater than `Fade Start`. Logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet.
members.fadeStart: Instanced-mesh distance fade. When `distanceFade` is on, instances shrink toward their base between `fadeStart` and `fadeEnd`, both model-space distances from the camera. Toggling the flag reloads the mesh (shader variant `Ifd`); the two distances are uniforms and can change without a reload. `Fade End` must be greater than `Fade Start`. Logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet.
members.getAABB: Useful for frustum culling, click picking, and physics proxy fitting.
members.getInstanceCustom: A `Vector4` of the instance at `index` that shader files read as `context.instance`, for a color, a growth stage or a random seed per instance (see Per-instance values). It is the `custom` field of InstanceData, `(0,0,0,0)` by default. The setter marks the instances for upload, so no updateInstances call is needed. It logs an error if the mesh is not instanced, and the getter then returns zero.
members.getNumSubmeshes: Returns the number of submeshes. Each submesh can have its own material, primitive type, and culling settings.
members.getVerticesAABB: Useful for frustum culling, click picking, and physics proxy fitting.
members.getWorldAABB: Useful for frustum culling, click picking, and physics proxy fitting.
members.instancedBillboard: Turns every instance to face the camera, the per-instance counterpart of Object.billboard. Both default to `false`, and `instancedCylindricalBillboard` only matters while `instancedBillboard` is on. The setters create the instanced mesh if it does not exist yet.
members.instancedCylindricalBillboard: Turns every instance to face the camera, the per-instance counterpart of Object.billboard. Both default to `false`, and `instancedCylindricalBillboard` only matters while `instancedBillboard` is on. The setters create the instanced mesh if it does not exist yet.
members.isMirror: The engine creates and drives the reflection camera internally and feeds its render target to the mesh's base texture — no camera setup is required. Set `receiveLights` to `false` for a reflection shown without surface shading. See Rendering Pipeline — Mirrors.
members.load: Uploads geometry and material resources to the GPU. Must be called after building or modifying geometry programmatically. Subclasses like `Sprite` call this internally when needed.
members.lodBias: Mesh detail levels. `lodEnabled` (default `true`) lets this mesh follow the scene's detail levels; turn it off to keep it at full detail, for example a hero asset whose silhouette must never change. Toggling it reloads the mesh. `lodBias` (default `1`) scales how far detail is kept: above 1 keeps the source longer, below 1 drops to a coarser level sooner.
members.lodEnabled: Mesh detail levels. `lodEnabled` (default `true`) lets this mesh follow the scene's detail levels; turn it off to keep it at full detail, for example a hero asset whose silhouette must never change. Toggling it reloads the mesh. `lodBias` (default `1`) scales how far detail is kept: above 1 keeps the source longer, below 1 drops to a coarser level sooner.
members.material: PBR material descriptor. Contains base color, metallic/roughness factors, normal map, emissive settings, and the shader with its parameter values.
members.maxInstances: Slots in the GPU instance buffer, `100` by default. Drawing clamps to it, but addInstance grows the cap as the list outgrows it — reloading the mesh each time — so the clamp only bites when the instance list is filled without going through `addInstance`. Set the capacity up front when the count is already known, to skip those reloads. Unlike the billboard setters, this one logs an error if the mesh is not instanced yet — call createInstancedMesh first.
members.primitiveType: GPU draw mode. Overloads are available per submesh.
members.receiveIBL: When `true`, the mesh samples image-based lighting: diffuse irradiance plus specular reflections on top of punctual lights. The source is the scene's Sky environment, a Reflection Probe whose volume covers the mesh, or both. Sky lighting needs a Sky entity with a cubemap texture; probes need none. Also requires Receive Lights enabled and surface normals.
members.receiveShadows: Shadow participation flags. Enabling both adds depth-map cost; disable on distant or small objects for performance.
members.removeMirror: The engine creates and drives the reflection camera internally and feeds its render target to the mesh's base texture — no camera setup is required. Set `receiveLights` to `false` for a reflection shown without surface shading. See Rendering Pipeline — Mirrors.
members.renderInReflectionProbes: Whether the mesh is drawn into ReflectionProbe captures. Turn it off when an object surrounds or sits on a probe and would otherwise show up inside its own reflection. Normal rendering is unaffected — this only controls the capture pass.
members.setAsMirror: The engine creates and drives the reflection camera internally and feeds its render target to the mesh's base texture — no camera setup is required. Set `receiveLights` to `false` for a reflection shown without surface shading. See Rendering Pipeline — Mirrors.
members.setInstanceCustom: A `Vector4` of the instance at `index` that shader files read as `context.instance`, for a color, a growth stage or a random seed per instance (see Per-instance values). It is the `custom` field of InstanceData, `(0,0,0,0)` by default. The setter marks the instances for upload, so no updateInstances call is needed. It logs an error if the mesh is not instanced, and the getter then returns zero.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube` (see Textures), on the material of every submesh or of one. The Texture can be a file, pixel data or a camera's render target, and an empty one draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without rebuilding the shader. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set on the material of `submesh`, the first without one, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the mesh's shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name (see Declaring parameters). They are stored on the materials: without a submesh a value goes to every submesh, and with one, as a `Vector4`, only to that submesh, so two submeshes can give the same shader different values. A narrower value leaves the remaining components at zero, and an `int` parameter takes the truncated value. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can be called every frame. Names the shader does not declare are kept but unused, and a parameter with no value reads the scene's value while the material inherits the scene default shader, else its declared default.
members.setTexture: Assigns the diffuse/base-color texture. Accepts a file path, raw `TextureData`, or a framebuffer render target.
members.shader: The shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the mesh draws with, as a project-relative path such as `"shaders/wave.glsl"`, or one of the engine's such as `"shaders/wind.glsl"`. It must be a `mesh` shader. The path is stored on the material of each submesh, so submeshes can draw with different shaders. Its hooks also run in the depth, shadow and G-buffer passes, so shadows, SSAO and reflections follow what it draws; see Mesh hooks.
members.transparent: `transparent` marks the mesh for the transparent render pass (sorted back-to-front). `autoTransparency` detects blending from the material (`BLEND`, or `AUTO` when the texture or factor is translucent) and enables the transparent pass automatically. A blended submesh keeps depth testing but disables depth writes in the colour pass so overlapping translucent surfaces composite correctly.
members.updateInstance: Replaces the data for an existing instance at `index`. Call updateInstances afterwards to sync changes to the GPU.
members.updateInstances: Uploads all pending instance data changes to the GPU vertex buffer. Must be called after any addInstance or updateInstance calls.
members.vertexOffsetMax: The longest distance, in world units, the shader's vertex offset moves a vertex. Longer offsets are clamped to it, and culling widens the mesh bounds and each instance's sphere by it, so moved geometry is not culled at the screen edge or out of a shadow cascade. `0` (default) clamps nothing and keeps the bounds of the mesh data. It belongs to the mesh, not to a material, so one value covers every submesh.

Mirror.description: A flat mesh that reflects the scene — a true planar reflection, used for mirrors, still water, and polished floors. Constructing a `Mirror` attaches a `MirrorComponent` to the entity; the engine creates and drives the reflection camera internally, so no camera or texture wiring is required.

members.normal: The reflecting surface direction in the mesh's local space. It is transformed by the entity's world rotation to build the mirror plane, so rotating the entity orients the reflection automatically.

Model.description: Loads and displays 3D model files in a scene. `Model` extends Mesh and adds support for loading OBJ and GLTF files (including binary GLB), and FBX files through the glTF conversion the editor makes of them, including skeletal animation (via `Animation` / `Bone`), blend-shape morph targets, and PBR materials.

members.findAnimation: Retrieve a skeletal or morph-target animation embedded in the loaded model. `getAnimation()` accesses by zero-based index; `findAnimation()` searches the animation entity name. GLTF import initializes that entity name from the clip name exported by the DCC tool, and an unnamed imported clip receives a generated name such as `"Animation 0"`. Both methods return an Animation object that can be started, stopped, and configured for looping.
members.getAnimation: Retrieve a skeletal or morph-target animation embedded in the loaded model. `getAnimation()` accesses by zero-based index; `findAnimation()` searches the animation entity name. GLTF import initializes that entity name from the clip name exported by the DCC tool, and an unnamed imported clip receives a generated name such as `"Animation 0"`. Both methods return an Animation object that can be started, stopped, and configured for looping.
members.getBone: Returns a Bone handle by joint name or by glTF node index (`id`). That integer is the node's index in the glTF file, which can differ from its ordinal in a skin's joint list. A `Bone` inherits Object so you can read and write its local transform to override the skeleton. For example, you can aim a character's head bone toward a target while the rest of the body plays a walk cycle.
members.getMorphWeight: Read or write the weight of a blend-shape morph target. Weights range from `0.0` (no influence) to `1.0` (full influence). Multiple morphs can be active simultaneously. Access by exported name or by zero-based index.
members.loadGLTF: Format-specific loaders. Use these when you want to be explicit about the format, or when the file extension is non-standard. `loadGLTF()` accepts both text `.gltf` and binary `.glb` files.
members.loadModel: Loads a 3D model file from disk. Doriax automatically detects the format based on file extension:
members.loadOBJ: Format-specific loaders. Use these when you want to be explicit about the format, or when the file extension is non-standard. `loadGLTF()` accepts both text `.gltf` and binary `.glb` files.
members.playAnimation: Switch the model's active clip with a smooth crossfade instead of an instant pose snap. `playAnimation()` fades out every other running clip on this model and fades the requested one in over `fadeTime` seconds; `stopAnimations()` fades all running clips out.
members.resetToBindPose: Resets every imported node (or, on the legacy skeleton path, every bone) back to the bind pose defined in the model file, clearing any programmatic or animation-driven overrides. Useful when switching between animations or when stopping all playback. A mesh part that was moved away from its file node keeps its transform, since the file's pose is relative to another parent.
members.setMorphWeight: Read or write the weight of a blend-shape morph target. Weights range from `0.0` (no influence) to `1.0` (full influence). Multiple morphs can be active simultaneously. Access by exported name or by zero-based index.
members.stopAnimations: Switch the model's active clip with a smooth crossfade instead of an instant pose snap. `playAnimation()` fades out every other running clip on this model and fades the requested one in over `fadeTime` seconds; `stopAnimations()` fades all running clips out.

OBB.description: An Oriented Bounding Box — a box whose axes can be rotated arbitrarily in world space. OBBs provide tighter fit than AABBs for non-axis-aligned objects at the cost of more complex intersection tests.

members.center: The box centre and the half-extents along each local axis.
members.closestPoint: Returns the point on or inside the OBB closest to `point`.
members.contains: Returns `true` if this OBB fully contains the given point or box.
members.distance: Distance from a point to the nearest surface of this OBB.
members.enclose: Expands the OBB to also contain another OBB or a point.
members.getCorner: `getCorner()` returns one corner, named by `OBB.CornerEnum` (`FAR_LEFT_BOTTOM`, `NEAR_RIGHT_TOP`, and so on). `getCorners()` returns all eight, in the order of those enum values. Lua gets them as a table of copies, so `corners[c + 1]` is `getCorner(c)`.
members.getCorners: `getCorner()` returns one corner, named by `OBB.CornerEnum` (`FAR_LEFT_BOTTOM`, `NEAR_RIGHT_TOP`, and so on). `getCorners()` returns all eight, in the order of those enum values. Lua gets them as a table of copies, so `corners[c + 1]` is `getCorner(c)`.
members.getOrientation: The rotation of the box as a quaternion. Lua reads and writes it through the `orientation` property.
members.halfExtents: The box centre and the half-extents along each local axis.
members.intersects: Intersection tests using the Separating Axis Theorem (SAT).
members.setAxes: Sets the three orthonormal local axes of the OBB. Can also be specified as a quaternion.
members.setOrientation: The rotation of the box as a quaternion. Lua reads and writes it through the `orientation` property.
members.squaredDistance: Distance from a point to the nearest surface of this OBB.
members.toAABB: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box that fully encloses this OBB.
members.toString: Returns a human-readable description of the OBB.
members.transform: Applies a transformation to the OBB.

Object.description: `Object` is the base class for all scene objects. It wraps an ECS entity and exposes the transform (position, rotation, scale), parent–child hierarchy, visibility, billboard orientation, and shortcuts to the physics body attachments.

members.addChild: Attaches `child` to this object's transform hierarchy. The child's `position`, `rotation`, and `scale` become relative to this object.
members.billboard: When `true`, the object's orientation is overridden each frame so it always faces the active camera. Position and scale are unaffected.
members.billboardRotation: An additional rotation applied on top of the billboard face-camera rotation. Use to offset or spin billboard sprites.
members.cylindricalBillboard: Constrains billboard rotation to the Y axis only (vertical axis). The object faces the camera horizontally but does not tilt up or down.
members.fakeBillboard: Fake billboard rotates the object to face the camera while keeping the local `position` offset in world space. Unlike a true billboard, the object moves as its parent moves but stays facing the camera.
members.getBody2D: Returns the Body2D physics handle for this object. Creates the body component if it does not already exist.
members.getBody3D: Returns the Body3D physics handle for this object. Creates the body component if it does not already exist.
members.getCharacter3D: Returns the Character3D handle for this object. Creates the character component if it does not already exist.
members.getRay: Constructs a Ray originating from this object's world position in the given world-space direction. Useful for raycasting from an object's location.
members.getWorldPosition: Returns the position of this object in world space, taking the full parent chain into account.
members.getWorldRotation: Returns the combined world-space rotation after applying all parent rotations.
members.getWorldScale: Returns the effective world-space scale, multiplied through the parent chain.
members.localMatrix: Provides direct access to the local-space transform matrix. Setting this overrides position/rotation/scale decomposed values. Useful for loading pre-computed transforms from GLTF animations or procedural geometry.
members.modelMatrix: Read-only world-space transform matrix, computed from the full parent chain. Updated by the transform system every frame.
members.moveDown: Control the draw/update order of this object among its siblings.
members.moveToBottom: Control the draw/update order of this object among its siblings.
members.moveToTop: Control the draw/update order of this object among its siblings.
members.moveUp: Control the draw/update order of this object among its siblings.
members.normalMatrix: Inverse transpose of the model matrix. Used in shaders to correctly transform surface normals when non-uniform scale is applied.
members.position: Local position relative to the parent object (or world origin if no parent). Changing position does not automatically update children — that is handled by the scene's transform system each frame.
members.removeBody2D: Destroys the 2D physics body attached to this object.
members.removeBody3D: Destroys the 3D physics body attached to this object.
members.removeCharacter3D: Destroys the 3D character attached to this object.
members.removeChild: Detaches `child` from this hierarchy. The child's world transform is preserved by converting it back to world-space values.
members.removeParent: Detaches this object from its parent and re-parents it to the scene root. The world transform is preserved.
members.rotation: Local rotation relative to the parent. The Euler overload uses the same default as `Quaternion(x, y, z)` — ZYX order (see Quaternion).
members.scale: Local scale relative to the parent.
members.setBillboard: Enables billboard mode. The three-argument overload allows setting `fake` and `cylindrical` flags in a single call. See billboard, fakeBillboard, and cylindricalBillboard.
members.setPosition: Sets local position. See position property.
members.setRotation: Sets local rotation. See rotation property.
members.setScale: Sets local scale. The single-float overload applies uniform scale on all axes.
members.setVisible: Shows or hides this object. Descendants are hidden with it but keep their own `visible` flag.
members.updateTransform: Forces an immediate recalculation of the world transform. The engine handles this automatically each frame; call only when you need an up-to-date transform outside the normal update order. Writing a transform from `onFixedUpdate` is one such case: the physics step reads the world transform, which is otherwise only refreshed once per frame.
members.visible: Hides or shows the object. Its children are hidden with it but keep their own flag, so showing the object again shows only the children that are visible themselves. `setVisibleOnly` is gone for the same reason: `setVisible` no longer touches the children's flags, so call it instead.
members.visibleInHierarchy: `true` when the object and all of its ancestors are visible. The render system refreshes it on each update, so right after a `setVisible` call it still holds the previous value.

Occluder2D.description: A shadow caster for 2D lights. An `Occluder2D` defines an outline (a quad derived from the entity's mesh, or a custom polygon) that blocks light from every shadow-enabled Light2D in the scene.

members.addVertex: Build a custom polygon outline in local space. Points are connected in order; with closed enabled the last point connects back to the first.
members.closed: Whether the polygon outline is a closed loop (last point connects to the first) or an open chain. Only relevant for the `POLYGON` shape — `AUTO_QUAD` is always closed.
members.enabled: Toggles the occluder without removing the component. Disabled occluders cast no shadows.
members.shape: Selects how the occluder outline is defined. See Occluder2DShape. Calling addVertex switches the shape to `POLYGON` automatically.

Panel.description: A draggable, resizable floating window panel. `Panel` extends Image with a header bar that can display a title, and an optional container area below it. Users can drag the header to move the panel, drag the edges to resize it, and click to bring it to the front of other panels.

members.hasHeader: Returns `true` if a header bar has been created (i.e. `setTitle()` has been called or a header texture has been set).
members.header: Configuration for the panel's header bar. `setHeaderMargin()` defines the pixel inset from the panel edges to where the header bar begins.
members.resizeMargin: The width in pixels of the invisible hit area at the panel edges that triggers resize drag. Default is `6`.
members.title: The window title shown in the header bar. Setting a non-empty title automatically creates child Text and Container entities for the header.

Particles.description: A GPU-accelerated particle emitter driven by the Action system. `Particles` handles birth, lifetime, movement, colour, and death for large numbers of small quads (sprites) to create effects such as fire, smoke, sparks, rain, and explosions.

members.addBurst: Bursts spawn a fixed number of particles at a specific time (in seconds) during the emitter's cycle, independent of rate. Useful for explosions.
members.addColorGradientStop: Defines a multi-stop colour gradient applied over the particle's lifetime instead of a simple two-point modifier. `addColorGradientStop()` adds one stop at `time` (0–1). `setColorGradientUseSRGB()` enables perceptually-linear interpolation through sRGB colour space.
members.clearBursts: Bursts spawn a fixed number of particles at a specific time (in seconds) during the emitter's cycle, independent of rate. Useful for explosions.
members.clearColorGradient: Defines a multi-stop colour gradient applied over the particle's lifetime instead of a simple two-point modifier. `addColorGradientStop()` adds one stop at `time` (0–1). `setColorGradientUseSRGB()` enables perceptually-linear interpolation through sRGB colour space.
members.emitter: When `true`, the particle system actively spawns new particles at the configured rate. Set to `false` to stop new emissions while allowing existing particles to finish their lifetime.
members.emitterShape: The spawn volume for new particles. See ParticleEmitterShape.
members.localSpace: When `true`, particle positions are in local object space — they move with the emitter entity. When `false` (default), positions are in world space — particles continue along their trajectories even after the emitter moves.
members.loop: When `true`, the particle system restarts automatically after all particles have died. When `false`, the system stops after the first complete emission cycle.
members.maxParticles: The maximum number of particles alive at any time. Increase this for denser effects; be mindful of GPU/CPU budget.
members.maxPerUpdate: Caps the number of new particles spawned in a single update tick. Prevents a very long delta time (e.g. after a frame spike) from spawning hundreds of particles in one frame.
members.rate: Number of new particles spawned per second while the emitter is active.
members.reset: Immediately destroys all live particles and resets the emitter to its initial state.
members.setAccelerationInitializer: Sets a constant per-particle acceleration (like gravity) applied from birth. Use `Vector3(0, -9.81f, 0)` to simulate gravity.
members.setAccelerationModifier: Animates the per-particle acceleration offset over its normalised lifetime.
members.setAlphaInitializer: Sets the initial opacity for each particle. `1.0` = fully opaque, `0.0` = invisible.
members.setAlphaModifier: Animates opacity over the particle's normalised lifetime. For a fade-out effect, use `fromTime=0, toTime=1, fromAlpha=1, toAlpha=0`.
members.setBursts: Bursts spawn a fixed number of particles at a specific time (in seconds) during the emitter's cycle, independent of rate. Useful for explosions.
members.setCirclePositionInitializer: Spawns particles on a flat circle in the XZ plane. `innerRadius` creates a ring.
members.setColorGradient: Defines a multi-stop colour gradient applied over the particle's lifetime instead of a simple two-point modifier. `addColorGradientStop()` adds one stop at `time` (0–1). `setColorGradientUseSRGB()` enables perceptually-linear interpolation through sRGB colour space.
members.setColorGradientUseSRGB: Defines a multi-stop colour gradient applied over the particle's lifetime instead of a simple two-point modifier. `addColorGradientStop()` adds one stop at `time` (0–1). `setColorGradientUseSRGB()` enables perceptually-linear interpolation through sRGB colour space.
members.setColorInitializer: Sets the particle's initial linear-space RGB colour. The range form randomises colour per particle.
members.setColorModifier: Lerps colour over the particle's normalised lifetime. Times are in `[0, 1]`.
members.setConePositionInitializer: Spawns particles inside a cone. `angle` is the half-angle of the cone (in degrees or radians depending on `Engine::useDegrees`), and `height` is its vertical extent.
members.setHemispherePositionInitializer: Spawns particles within the upper hemisphere (Y ≥ 0). Useful for upward explosions or fountain effects.
members.setLifeInitializer: Set how long (in seconds) each particle lives. The two-argument form randomises lifetime between `minLife` and `maxLife`.
members.setPositionInitializer: Sets the spawn position (or random range) relative to the emitter. For Box shape, `minPosition` and `maxPosition` define the box corners.
members.setPositionModifier: Adds a position offset over the particle's normalised lifetime (0 = birth, 1 = death). The `fromTime` and `toTime` values are in the `[0, 1]` range. An optional EaseType controls interpolation.
members.setRotationInitializer: Sets the initial rotation of each particle. The scalar overload takes an angle (degrees or radians per `Engine::useDegrees`) around the Z axis for 2D-style billboard rotation.
members.setRotationModifier: Animates rotation over the particle's normalised lifetime.
members.setScaleInitializer: Sets the initial scale at birth. Use the `Vector3` overload for non-uniform scale.
members.setScaleModifier: Animates the particle's scale over its normalised lifetime. Useful for particles that shrink as they die.
members.setSizeInitializer: Sets the initial uniform size of each particle in world units.
members.setSizeModifier: Animates particle size over its normalised lifetime.
members.setSpherePositionInitializer: Spawns particles within a sphere of the given radius. `innerRadius` creates a hollow sphere (donut shape) — particles only spawn in the shell between `innerRadius` and `radius`.
members.setSpriteInitializer: Sets which sprite atlas frame each particle shows at birth. The vector form provides an explicit list to pick from randomly; the two-integer form picks a random frame in the range.
members.setSpriteModifier: Plays `frames` in order between `fromTime` and `toTime` of each particle's life, in seconds, ending on the last frame. With the default linear easing each frame gets an equal share of that time.
members.setVelocityInitializer: Sets the initial velocity (units per second) at birth. The range form picks a random velocity for each particle between `minVelocity` and `maxVelocity`.
members.setVelocityModifier: Interpolates the particle's velocity offset over its normalised lifetime. Times are in the `[0, 1]` range.

Plane.description: An infinite plane in 3D space represented in the form `n·x + d = 0`, where `n` is the unit normal vector and `d` is the signed distance from the origin.

members.getDistance: Returns the signed distance from `rkPoint` to the plane. Positive values are on the `normal` side.
members.getSide: Determines which side of the plane a point or volume is on. Useful for frustum culling and portal rendering.
members.normalize: Normalises the plane equation so that `normal` has unit length.
members.normalized: Normalises the plane equation so that `normal` has unit length.
members.projectVector: Projects `v` onto the plane, returning the component of `v` tangent to the plane.
members.redefine: Recomputes the plane from three non-collinear points or from a normal and a point.

Points.description: Renders a collection of 3D billboard points (sprites). Each point is a camera-facing quad with an individual position, colour, size, rotation, and optional texture atlas frame. Useful for particle-like effects, star fields, or any situation where a large number of individually controlled sprites is needed.

members.addSpriteFrame: Defines a named atlas frame for use with the `textureRect` field of PointData. This enables different points to show different sub-regions of the same texture atlas.
members.autoTransparency: Controls transparency rendering for this points object. See Mesh for details.
members.getNumPoints: Returns the current number of points.
members.getPoint: Returns a reference to the `PointData` at `index`. Modify in-place then call `updatePoints()`.
members.isPointVisible: Show or hide individual points without removing them from the buffer.
members.load: Explicitly initialises the GPU buffer. This method is C++ only and is normally optional because the render system initialises points automatically.
members.maxPoints: Pre-allocates GPU buffer space for this many points.
members.setPointVisible: Show or hide individual points without removing them from the buffer.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without reloading the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.setTexture: Sets the texture used for all points. When using a texture atlas, call addSpriteFrame to define the atlas regions.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `points` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the points draw with, such as `"shaders/sparks.glsl"`. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultPointsShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. See Custom Shaders.
members.transparent: Controls transparency rendering for this points object. See Mesh for details.
members.updatePoints: Uploads changes to the GPU. Must be called after any modification.

members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without reloading the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `ui` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the polygon draws with, such as `"shaders/glow.glsl"`. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultUIShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. It is the `shader` field of UIComponent; see Custom Shaders.

PositionAction.description: Animates the `position` property of its target object, moving it from a start position to an end position over a fixed duration. Works in both 2D and 3D scenes.

members.setAction: Configures the tween. `startPosition` and `endPosition` are world-space coordinates. `duration` is in seconds.

PostProcessPass.description: One entry of a scene's post-process chain: the shader file to run over the finished image, whether it runs, and the values and textures of the parameters it declares. Passes are plain values — build them, then hand the whole chain to Scene.postProcessPasses. To change a value on a chain that is already running, use Scene.setPostProcessUniform, which does not rebuild the chain.

members.enabled: Whether the pass runs. A disabled pass keeps its shader and values, and is still exported, so it can be turned back on at runtime with Scene.setPostProcessPassEnabled.
members.setTexture: Texture parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube` (see Textures), keyed by name and stored in `textures`. An empty texture draws the declared default. Like the values, a texture reaches the scene when the chain is set again, but a changed texture rebuilds the chain; on a running chain, Scene.setPostProcessTexture sets one directly. `getTexture` returns the stored texture, empty when none.
members.setUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, keyed by name and stored in `uniforms`. A name the shader does not declare is stored but unused, and a parameter with no value reads its declared default. A narrower value leaves the remaining components at zero. These edit the pass value only; the scene picks the change up when the chain is set again (a value-only change keeps the compiled chain).
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `postprocess` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`), such as `"shaders/vignette.glsl"`. Its `getColor` hook runs over the finished image and receives the previous pass at each pixel. Empty runs the built-in passthrough, which is also what a shader that fails to build falls back to.

Progressbar.description: A UI widget that displays a value in the `[0, 1]` range as a filled bar. The bar can grow horizontally (left to right) or vertically (bottom to top). Both the background and the fill area support 9-patch textures and independent tint colours.

members.getFillObject: Returns the child Image entity that renders the fill area. Use this to set fill properties directly if you need more control than the convenience setters provide.
members.setFillColor: Tint colour applied to the fill texture.
members.setFillMargin: Pixel offset between the background edges and the fill image.
members.setFillTexture: Sets the texture for the fill portion of the bar.
members.value: Current fill amount. `0.0` = empty, `1.0` = full. Clamped to `[0, 1]`.

Quaternion.description: Represents a rotation in 3D space using the quaternion formalism. Quaternions avoid gimbal lock, support smooth slerp interpolation, and are more numerically stable than Euler-angle representations for concatenated rotations.

members.dot: Returns the dot product between two quaternions. Values near `1` indicate similar orientations; near `-1` indicate opposite orientations.
members.fromAngle: Constructs a 2D-style rotation around the Z axis. Convenience for 2D scenes.
members.fromAngleAxis: Constructs the quaternion from an angle-axis representation. Useful for arbitrary-axis rotations.
members.fromAxes: Builds the quaternion from an orthonormal basis of three axes.
members.fromEuler: Constructs the quaternion from Euler angles. Angles are in degrees if `Engine::useDegrees` is `true`.
members.getEuler: Extracts Euler angles from this quaternion in the specified rotation order.
members.getPitch: Extracts the roll (Z), pitch (X), or yaw (Y) angle component.
members.getRoll: Extracts the roll (Z), pitch (X), or yaw (Y) angle component.
members.getRotationMatrix: Converts this quaternion to a `Matrix4` rotation matrix.
members.getYaw: Extracts the roll (Z), pitch (X), or yaw (Y) angle component.
members.inverse: `inverse()` returns the inverse (safe for any non-zero quaternion). `unitInverse()` is faster but only correct for unit quaternions.
members.lookRotation: Returns a rotation whose local +Z axis faces `forward`, keeping local +Y close to `up` (`Vector3::UNIT_Y` by default). A zero `forward` returns `IDENTITY`. Cameras look down -Z, so for a camera call disableTarget and pass `position - target`.
members.nlerp: Normalised linear interpolation. Cheaper than `slerp()` but not constant-speed; suitable for small angular differences or when speed uniformity is not critical.
members.norm: Returns the squared length of the quaternion. A normalised quaternion has `norm()` = `1`.
members.normalize: `normalize()` scales the quaternion in-place to unit length. `normalized()` returns a new unit-length copy.
members.normalizeL: Normalises in-place and returns the original norm.
members.normalized: `normalize()` scales the quaternion in-place to unit length. `normalized()` returns a new unit-length copy.
members.slerp: Spherical linear interpolation. `t=0` returns `q1`, `t=1` returns `q2`. When `shortestPath` is `true`, the interpolation always takes the shorter arc.
members.squad: Spherical cubic (SQUAD) interpolation between two quaternions `rkP` and `rkQ` with inner control points `rkA` and `rkB`. Used for smooth keyframe animation.
members.unitInverse: `inverse()` returns the inverse (safe for any non-zero quaternion). `unitInverse()` is faster but only correct for unit quaternions.
members.xAxis: Returns the local X, Y, or Z axis expressed in world space — equivalent to rotating the corresponding unit vector by this quaternion.
members.yAxis: Returns the local X, Y, or Z axis expressed in world space — equivalent to rotating the corresponding unit vector by this quaternion.
members.zAxis: Returns the local X, Y, or Z axis expressed in world space — equivalent to rotating the corresponding unit vector by this quaternion.

Ray.description: A ray defined by an origin point and a direction/length vector. Used for raycasting — detecting which objects lie along the ray. Doriax supports raycasts against geometric volumes (AABB, OBB, Sphere, Plane), against the physics simulation (Body2D / Body3D), and against the bounds of every mesh in a scene, which needs no physics at all.

members.direction: `origin` is the start of the ray. `direction` is both the normalised direction and the maximum reach (its magnitude = ray length). Use `Camera::screenToRay()` to generate a ray from a screen pixel.
members.getPoint: Returns `origin + direction * distance`. Hits report `distance` as a fraction of the ray, from 0 at `origin` to 1 at `origin + direction`, so `getPoint(hit.distance)` is the hit point.
members.intersects: Multiple overloads for different collision targets:
members.origin: `origin` is the start of the ray. `direction` is both the normalised direction and the maximum reach (its magnitude = ray length). Use `Camera::screenToRay()` to generate a ray from a screen pixel.

Rect.description: An axis-aligned rectangle defined by an origin `(x, y)` and size `(width, height)`. Used throughout the engine for screen regions, texture atlas frames, viewport definitions, and UI layouts.

members.contains: Returns `true` if `point` lies inside this rectangle (inclusive).
members.fitOnRect: Scales and positions this rect to fit inside `rect` while preserving the aspect ratio. Modifies in-place and returns `*this`.
members.getVector: Returns the rect as a `Vector4(x, y, width, height)`.
members.height: The four components of the rectangle.
members.isNormalized: Returns `true` if all components are in the `[0, 1]` range, as expected for normalised UV or NDC coordinates.
members.isZero: Returns `true` if all four components are zero.
members.setRect: Sets all four components at once.
members.width: The four components of the rectangle.
members.x: The four components of the rectangle.
members.y: The four components of the rectangle.

ReflectionProbe.description: A local reflection environment. Meshes inside the probe's box-shaped influence volume sample its cubemap (box-projected, so reflections stay anchored to the volume) instead of the global sky environment. Meshes need Receive IBL and Receive Lights enabled to pick probes up.

members.blendDistance: Fade band inside the box edges where the probe blends into the sky IBL, hiding the seam at the volume boundary. Runtime blending is limited to the box's smallest half-extent.
members.boxOffset: The influence volume, in the entity's local space. The box is world-axis-aligned, centred on the entity plus `boxOffset`, and scaled by the entity's world scale. The cubemap is always captured at the entity origin, not the offset centre.
members.boxSize: The influence volume, in the entity's local space. The box is world-axis-aligned, centred on the entity plus `boxOffset`, and scaled by the entity's world scale. The cubemap is always captured at the entity origin, not the offset centre.
members.farClip: Clip planes of the capture cameras.
members.includeSky: Whether the sky (and scene background colour) appears in runtime captures.
members.intensity: Multiplier on the probe's reflection contribution.
members.mode: Whether the probe is static or re-captures at runtime. Changing the mode restarts any in-flight capture.
members.nearClip: Clip planes of the capture cameras.
members.priority: When influence boxes overlap, the higher-priority probe wins; on a tie, the probe whose centre is nearest the mesh wins.
members.refresh: Requests a new capture (or re-bake of the authored cubemap), regardless of mode and update mode. This is what the editor's Refresh Probe button calls, and the way to update a `MANUAL` probe from gameplay code.
members.resolution: Capture cubemap face size, clamped to 16–1024 at capture time. Changing it restarts any in-flight capture. The capture is prefiltered into 128-pixel faces like an authored cubemap, so sizes above 128 make reflections smoother, not sharper.
members.setTexture: Assigns the authored cubemap used by `STATIC` probes — six face image paths, or a single cross-layout image. Authored cubemaps are GGX-prefiltered like the sky environment, so rough surfaces get correct blurry reflections.
members.setTextures: Assigns the authored cubemap used by `STATIC` probes — six face image paths, or a single cross-layout image. Authored cubemaps are GGX-prefiltered like the sky environment, so rough surfaces get correct blurry reflections.
members.updateInterval: Seconds between captures for `INTERVAL` update mode.
members.updateMode: When a `DYNAMIC` probe re-captures. Ignored by static probes.

RotationAction.description: Animates the `rotation` property of its target object using quaternion spherical linear interpolation (slerp) between a start and end rotation. A slerp takes the short way between two rotations, so it never turns more than half a turn; setSpinAction turns by any angle instead, for full spins.

members.setAction: Configures the tween. `startRotation` and `endRotation` are quaternion values. `duration` is in seconds.
members.setSpinAction: Turns `startRotation` by `angle` around `axis` over `duration` seconds. The angle can be any size, so `360` is a full turn and `720` two turns, and the axis is in the frame of `startRotation`. The angle uses the engine's angle unit (degrees by default). In the editor, check Spin in the RotationAction component and set its Axis and Angle.

ScaleAction.description: Animates the `scale` property of its target object, interpolating between a start scale and an end scale over a fixed duration.

members.setAction: Configures the tween. `startScale` and `endScale` are scale vectors. `duration` is in seconds.

Scene.description: A `Scene` is the root container for all objects, systems, and resources in a project. It manages the active camera, background color, global illumination, shadow settings, mesh detail levels, the optional depth prepass, and the update/draw lifecycle. You typically create one or more scenes at startup and set the active one with `Engine::setScene`.

members.ambientLight2DColor: Part of setAmbientLight2D. Controls the tint of the 2D ambient light.
members.ambientLight2DIntensity: Part of setAmbientLight2D. Controls the brightness of the 2D ambient light applied to 2D-lit objects. Defaults to `1.0` (fully lit), so a scene looks unchanged until you dim it.
members.backgroundColor: Background clear color for the scene, in RGBA [0, 1] range. Convenience overloads accept `(r, g, b)` or `(r, g, b, a)` floats directly.
members.canReceiveUIEvents: Returns `true` if this scene is currently the topmost scene that is able to receive UI pointer events. The engine calls this internally to route events to the correct scene layer.
members.defaultLinesShader: Scene default `lines` shader for Lines components without a shader of their own. Same semantics as defaultMeshShader.
members.defaultMeshShader: Scene default `mesh` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`), as a project-relative path such as `"shaders/toon.glsl"`. Every submesh whose material has no shader of its own uses it; an empty string (default) means the engine built-in. A shader set on the material with Mesh.setShader always takes priority. Changing the value reloads the meshes. Its parameter values can be set for the whole scene with setDefaultShaderUniform. In C++, `setDefaultCustomShader(ShaderType type, path)` and `getDefaultCustomShader(type)` reach this and the other five defaults by type. See Custom Shaders — Scene default shaders.
members.defaultPointsShader: Scene default `points` shader for Points components without a shader of their own. Same semantics as defaultMeshShader.
members.defaultSkyShader: Scene default `sky` shader for a Sky component without a shader of its own. Same semantics as defaultMeshShader.
members.defaultUIShader: Scene default `ui` shader for UI components without a shader of their own. Same semantics as defaultMeshShader.
members.defaultWaterShader: Scene default `water` shader for Water components without a shader of their own. Same semantics as defaultMeshShader. Such a water uses it for both hooks, the surface and the underwater fade.
members.depthPrepassEnabled: Writes a depth-only pass for the main camera before the opaque colour draws, so overlapping pixels fail the depth test instead of running the lit shader. Off by default. Toggling it reloads meshes (the prepass pipelines are built with each mesh).
members.destroy: Tears down all subsystems and destroys every entity in the scene. Called automatically by the engine when the scene is removed from the stack.
members.draw: Triggers a render pass for this scene. Normally called by the engine each frame; use only for custom render pipelines.
members.enableUIEvents: Per-scene override for UI event routing. See UIEventState.
members.fixedResolutionEnabled: Renders the main camera into an internal buffer of fixedResolutionWidth × fixedResolutionHeight and upscales the result to the view rect, instead of rendering at the window's native resolution. Takes effect only when this scene is the Engine main scene; scenes added as layers always render at native resolution. Letterboxing, input mapping, and object coordinates keep following the canvas and scaling mode. In the editor, the fixed resolution is applied during play mode only. Toggling at runtime rebuilds the scene's render pipelines, which may cause a brief hitch — prefer changing the size instead. See Multiple Resolutions.
members.fixedResolutionFilter: Sampling filter used when the fixed-resolution image is upscaled to the view rect: `TextureFilter::NEAREST` (default) keeps hard pixel edges for a pixel-art look; `TextureFilter::LINEAR` interpolates smoothly, which suits fixed resolution used purely as a performance measure.
members.fixedUpdate: Runs one fixed-step update for physics and other time-sensitive systems. `dt` equals Engine::updateTime. Normally called by the engine.
members.getCamera: Returns the entity handle of the currently active camera.
members.getRenderCamera: Returns the camera the scene is drawn from: the view camera when one is set, otherwise the active camera.
members.globalIlluminationColor: Part of setGlobalIllumination. Controls the tint of the ambient light (linear color, [0,1] per channel).
members.globalIlluminationIntensity: Part of setGlobalIllumination. Controls the brightness of the ambient light applied uniformly across the scene.
members.gravity2D: Gravity of the 2D physics world (Box2D), in meters per second squared. Affects every dynamic Body2D in the scene, scaled per body by gravityScale. Independent from gravity3D. Changing it at runtime does not wake sleeping bodies. Forwards to the scene's PhysicsSystem. Default `(0, -9.81)`.
members.gravity3D: Gravity of the 3D physics world (Jolt), in meters per second squared. Affects every dynamic Body3D in the scene, scaled per body by gravityFactor. Independent from gravity2D. Changing it at runtime does not wake sleeping bodies. Forwards to the scene's PhysicsSystem. Default `(0, -9.81, 0)`.
members.isEnableUIEvents: Returns `true` if UI events are enabled for this scene (either via explicit `ENABLED` state or engine default).
members.lightState: Controls whether the render system activates the lighting pass. See LightState.
members.load: Initializes the scene subsystems. Called automatically by the engine when the scene is added via `Engine::setScene` or `Engine::addSceneLayer`. Only call manually when managing scenes outside the engine lifecycle.
members.meshLodEnabled: Scene-wide mesh detail levels. `meshLodEnabled` (default `false`) turns them on: each mesh gets simplified index ranges and draws one once its geometric error projects below `meshLodThreshold` screen pixels (default `1`). While it is off no levels are built, and turning it off frees their GPU buffers. The threshold is clamped to `≥ 0`. Changing either takes effect immediately; a mesh can opt out with lodEnabled.
members.meshLodThreshold: Scene-wide mesh detail levels. `meshLodEnabled` (default `false`) turns them on: each mesh gets simplified index ranges and draws one once its geometric error projects below `meshLodThreshold` screen pixels (default `1`). While it is off no levels are built, and turning it off frees their GPU buffers. The threshold is clamped to `≥ 0`. Changing either takes effect immediately; a mesh can opt out with lodEnabled.
members.postProcessPasses: Ordered chain of fullscreen post-process passes run over the scene's finished image, on the main camera only. Each entry is a PostProcessPass with the shader file to run, an enable flag, and the values and textures of the parameters it declares. In Lua the property is a 1-based sequence of `PostProcessPass` values (a copy — assign it back to apply changes); build the chain as a sequence (a `{...}` literal or `table.insert`), whose array order is the pass order, and note that `pass_index` arguments such as setPostProcessUniform count from 0.
members.removeSubscriptionsByTag: Removes all event subscriptions whose tag string contains `substring`. Used to clean up callbacks belonging to a destroyed script or component.
members.setAmbientLight2D: Sets the ambient light for the 2D lighting path (see Light2D). Every Light2D adds on top of this base level, so dim the ambient to make 2D lights visible. Separate from setGlobalIllumination, which drives the 3D PBR ambient.
members.setBackgroundColor: Sets the clear color used before rendering the scene each frame.
members.setCamera: Sets the active camera for this scene. Only one camera can be active at a time. Pass the `Camera` object or its underlying `Entity` handle.
members.setDefaultShaderUniform: Scene values for the parameters the scene default shader of `type` declares (see ShaderType), by name. Every material or component that inherits that default reads them for the parameters it does not set itself; a value set on it with setShaderUniform wins. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded blocks, so it can run every frame. A narrower value leaves the remaining components at zero, and a parameter with no value on either side reads its declared default. A type without a scene default is ignored. `getDefaultShaderUniform` returns the scene's stored value, zero when unset; `removeDefaultShaderUniform` drops it and returns whether it existed. The values stay when the default shader changes, so a shader with the same parameter names picks them up. See Custom Shaders — Scene default shaders.
members.setGlobalIllumination: Sets the ambient (global illumination) light for the scene. Intensity scales brightness; color tints the light. Flat-shaded or unlit materials are not affected.
members.setLightState: Overrides automatic lighting detection. See LightState.
members.setPostProcessPassEnabled: Turns the pass at `index` on or off. A change rebuilds the chain on the next frame (the compiled shader is kept, so it is cheap, but not something to toggle every frame). An index past the chain logs an error; `isPostProcessPassEnabled` returns `false` for it.
members.setPostProcessTexture: Sets a texture parameter of the pass at `index` (0 = first pass of postProcessPasses), by the name its shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`. An empty texture draws the declared default. A change rebuilds the chain on the next frame, so it is not something to call every frame. An index past the chain logs an error and is ignored. `getPostProcessTexture` returns the stored texture, empty when none or when the index is past the chain.
members.setPostProcessUniform: Sets one parameter of the pass at `index` (0 = first pass of postProcessPasses), by the name its shader declares with `#pragma param`. Only the uploaded block is rewritten, and the chain is not rebuilt, so it can run every frame. A narrower value leaves the remaining components at zero; a parameter with no value reads its declared default. An index past the chain logs an error and is ignored. `getPostProcessUniform` returns the stored value, zero when unset; `removePostProcessUniform` drops it (the parameter reads its declared default again) and returns whether it existed.
members.setViewCamera: Draws the scene from `camera` instead of the active camera, while getCamera keeps returning the active one, so scripts, audio, and UI events are unaffected. Effects tied to the main camera (shadows, SSAO, SSR, post-processing, terrain and mesh detail) follow the view camera. Pass `NULL_ENTITY` to draw from the active camera again. The editor uses it for its detached camera.
members.shadow2DQuality: Filter quality of 2D light shadows (PCF taps along the 1D polar shadow map). More taps smooth the same penumbra width (set per light by Light2D — shadowSoftness), removing banding on wide penumbras. Changing it takes effect immediately (no shader rebuild).
members.shadowQuality: Filter quality of 3D shadow map edges (PCF kernel size, applied instantly with no shader rebuild):
members.ssaoBias: View-space depth bias that prevents self-occlusion artifacts (acne) on flat surfaces. Increase slightly if flat areas appear dirty; keep small to preserve fine contact detail.
members.ssaoDebug: Debug aid: when enabled, lit meshes output the raw screen-space AO buffer as grayscale instead of their shaded color, so you can inspect and tune the occlusion directly. Not serialized.
members.ssaoEnabled: Enables screen-space ambient occlusion. SSAO darkens the ambient/indirect lighting (IBL or global illumination) in creases and contact areas; it does not affect direct light. Toggling it recompiles lit mesh shaders. Applies to the main camera; terrain is currently excluded.
members.ssaoHalfResolution: Computes and blurs the occlusion at half the width and height, for about a quarter of the cost, and lit meshes upsample it. The depth pre-pass stays at full size. AO comes out a little softer. Default `false`.
members.ssaoIntensity: Strength of the effect, applied as an exponent on the occlusion factor — higher values darken occluded areas more.
members.ssaoRadius: View-space sampling radius (world units). Larger values gather occlusion from farther surfaces (broader, softer AO); smaller values keep it to tight contact creases.
members.ssrBlur: Glossy blur amount in `[0..1]`. `0` keeps mirror-sharp reflections; higher values blur the reflection in proportion to each surface's roughness. Default `0.0`.
members.ssrDebugMode: Debug visualization of the SSR G-buffer, rendered full-screen: `0` off, `1` reflection buffer, `2` normal, `3` roughness, `4` metallic, `5` albedo, `6` IBL specular. Not serialized.
members.ssrEnabled: Enables screen-space reflections. SSR reflects on-screen geometry by marching the camera depth/G-buffer, and where it finds a hit it replaces the surface's environment reflection (the IBL sky or a reflection probe) rather than adding to it, falling back to that reflection where the ray misses. Requires a framebuffer destination (editor viewport, render-to-texture camera, or engine framebuffer) and applies to the main camera. Toggling it reloads meshes to build the G-buffer shaders.
members.ssrIntensity: Overall reflection strength multiplier applied in the composite. Default `1.0`.
members.ssrMaxDistance: Maximum reflection ray length in view-space units. Longer rays catch more distant reflections at higher cost. Default `8.0`.
members.ssrMaxSteps: Linear march sample count. Higher gives sharper, longer reflections (and helps thin contacts register) at more cost. Default `48`.
members.ssrThickness: Depth-compare tolerance (view-space units) for accepting a ray hit. Smaller is stricter; larger fills gaps but can smear at object contacts. Default `0.5`.
members.update: Runs one variable-step update for all subscribed systems. `dt` is the frame delta in seconds. Normally called by the engine.
members.updateCameraSize: Recalculates the active camera's projection to match the current canvas size. Called automatically when the canvas changes; call manually after resizing the viewport from script.

SceneManager.description: A registry for named scene stacks that lets you switch between scenes at runtime. A scene stack consists of one main Scene plus zero or more layer scenes (see Engine::addSceneLayer).

members.addChildScene: Add or remove a scene stack as layers on top of the running scenes without a full transition — ideal for overlaying a UI scene (pause menu, dialog) on top of a game scene.
members.cancelPreload: `preloadScene` loads the textures, sounds and models of a scene stack in the background while the current scene keeps running, so a later `loadScene` finds them ready and only has to build the scene. Call it early, for example when the player gets close to the exit door. It returns `false` for an unknown scene.
members.clearAll: Unregisters all scenes. Used by the editor when resetting state. Does not destroy scene objects.
members.getCurrentSceneId: Returns the ID or name of the most recently loaded scene.
members.getCurrentSceneName: Returns the ID or name of the most recently loaded scene.
members.getLoadingDelay: Seconds the loading scene covers the old scenes before they are replaced. Default `0`. The old scenes keep running below it until then, which leaves time for a fade in (a script on the loading scene can raise its alpha from `0` to `1` over the delay) and for their last sounds, such as a button click, which stop when the scenes are deleted.
members.getLoadingProgress: `isLoading` is `true` from a `loadScene` call until the new stack has loaded its resources and every hold is released, with or without a loading scene. It is already `true` while the new stack's scripts are constructed, and for the start scene too. To start gameplay once the level is ready, handle `Engine::onSceneLoaded` instead of polling it.
members.getLoadingSceneId: Sets a registered scene stack as the loading screen that `loadScene` shows over every transition, the start scene included. An empty name or `0` turns it off. Returns `false` if the scene is unknown. Exported games and the editor's Play set it from Project Settings → General → Loading, so most projects never call it.
members.getLoadingTimeout: Seconds a load waits without progress before it gives up. Default `5`. It applies to the loading scene's own resources before the switch, and to the new stack after it, which logs a warning naming what did not load. The clock restarts every time another resource finishes, so a slow load that keeps moving is never cut short.
members.getPreloadProgress: `preloadScene` loads the textures, sounds and models of a scene stack in the background while the current scene keeps running, so a later `loadScene` finds them ready and only has to build the scene. Call it early, for example when the player gets close to the exit door. It returns `false` for an unknown scene.
members.getSceneCount: Returns all registered scene names, or the total number of registered scenes.
members.getSceneId: Look up a scene's numeric ID by name, or its name by ID. Returns `0` / `""` if not found.
members.getSceneName: Look up a scene's numeric ID by name, or its name by ID. Returns `0` / `""` if not found.
members.getSceneNames: Returns all registered scene names, or the total number of registered scenes.
members.getScenePtr: Associates a live `Scene*` pointer with a registered scene ID.
