Used when one scene needs to reference entities in another scene (cross-scene entity resolution), and by an add factory to hand `addChildScene` the scenes it created. `getScenePtr` returns `nullptr` (`nil` in Lua) for an ID with no scene.
members.holdLoading: `holdLoading` keeps the current load open after the new stack has loaded: the loading scene stays on screen and `isLoading` stays `true` until every hold is released. Returns `false`, and holds nothing, when no load is running. Each successful `holdLoading` needs one `releaseLoading`.
members.isCoveredByLoading: `true` for a running scene below the shown loading scene. Such a scene gets no UI input, but its scripts still receive engine input events, so a script can check this to ignore keys while its scene is covered.
members.isLoadPending: `true` between a deferred `loadScene` call and the frame that replaces the old stack, loading delay included. Lua reads it as the `SceneManager.loadPending` property.
members.isLoading: `isLoading` is `true` from a `loadScene` call until the new stack has loaded its resources and every hold is released, with or without a loading scene. It is already `true` while the new stack's scripts are constructed, and for the start scene too. To start gameplay once the level is ready, handle `Engine::onSceneLoaded` instead of polling it.
members.loadScene: Loads a registered scene stack by name or ID, performing a full scene transition. members.releaseLoading: `holdLoading` keeps the current load open after the new stack has loaded: the loading scene stays on screen and `isLoading` stays `true` until every hold is released. Returns `false`, and holds nothing, when no load is running. Each successful `holdLoading` needs one `releaseLoading`.

Used when one scene needs to reference entities in another scene (cross-scene entity resolution), and by an add factory to hand `addChildScene` the scenes it created. `getScenePtr` returns `nullptr` (`nil` in Lua) for an ID with no scene.

ScriptBase.description: The base class for all C++ gameplay scripts attached to entities. To create a component script in C++, inherit from `ScriptBase` and register engine events with `REGISTER_ENGINE_EVENT` (there are no virtual `update` overrides).

members.entity: The scene this script belongs to, and the entity it is attached to. Use these to access Object transforms, add/remove components, or query the ECS.
members.scene: The scene this script belongs to, and the entity it is attached to. Use these to access Object transforms, add/remove components, or query the ECS.

Scrollbar.description: A UI scrollbar widget. The scrollbar consists of a track (the background Image) and a draggable bar handle (a child Image). Both can have independent textures and tint colours. The current scroll position is reported through the `onChange` callback.

members.barSize: The relative size of the draggable handle as a fraction of the track length, in `[0, 1]`. Larger values represent a proportionally large viewport relative to the content (e.g. `0.5` means the viewport covers half the content).
members.getBarObject: Returns the child Image handle entity for the draggable bar.
members.onChange: Called whenever the scroll position changes. `value` is in `[0, 1]` where `0` is the start of the track and `1` is the end.
members.setBarColor: Tint colour applied to the bar handle texture.
members.setBarMargin: Pixel offset between the track edges and the bar handle.
members.setBarPatchMargin: 9-patch insets for the bar handle image.
members.setBarTexture: Sets the texture for the bar handle.
members.step: Snap increment in `[0, 1]`. When non-zero, the scroll position snaps to multiples of this value. `0` means continuous scrolling.

members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without reloading the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `sky` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the sky draws with, such as `"shaders/dayNight.glsl"`. Its `getColor` hook receives the cube map sample times the sky's color and returns the color drawn. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultSkyShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. See Custom Shaders.

Sound.description: Plays audio clips in a scene, supporting both 2D and 3D positional audio. `Sound` wraps the SoLoud audio engine, giving you precise control over playback state, volume, pitch, panning, looping, 3D attenuation and Doppler effect.

members.attenuationModel: Select the distance-attenuation algorithm for this 3D source. See SoundAttenuation for the available values.
members.attenuationRolloffFactor: Scales how aggressively the attenuation model reduces volume with distance. Higher values mean faster roll-off. The exact meaning depends on the attenuationModel in use.
members.clockedSound: When enabled, SoLoud plays the sound in clocked mode. This keeps multiple streamed sounds synchronised to the engine's update tick, which is important when mixing music with synchronised sound effects. Has no effect on loaded WAV/OGG samples (`Wav`).
members.destroySound: Unloads the audio data and frees the SoLoud voice slot. Call this when the sound is no longer needed to free memory immediately without destroying the entity.
members.dopplerFactor: Controls the intensity of the Doppler pitch shift for this 3D source. `0.0` disables Doppler; `1.0` is physically accurate; values above `1.0` exaggerate the effect. Requires `sound3D` to be `true`.
members.getLength: `getLength()` returns the total duration of the loaded clip in seconds. `getPlayingTime()` returns the current playback cursor position in seconds.
members.getObject: Returns the `Object` component of this sound entity. Use this to set the world-space position for 3D audio or to attach the sound to a parent entity.
members.getPlayingTime: `getLength()` returns the total duration of the loaded clip in seconds. `getPlayingTime()` returns the current playback cursor position in seconds.
members.loadSound: Loads an audio file from disk. Supported formats depend on the SoLoud build bundled with Doriax (WAV, OGG, FLAC, MP3, and others). Returns `1` once the file is loaded, and `0` while it is still loading with async loading, when it failed, or before the view is ready. Loading a different file replaces the current one.
members.looping: When `true`, the clip restarts from loopingPoint after it finishes.
members.loopingPoint: Position in seconds at which the clip restarts when looping is `true`. Defaults to `0.0` (beginning of the clip).
members.maxDistance: Distance thresholds used by the attenuationModel when `sound3D` is `true`.
members.minDistance: Distance thresholds used by the attenuationModel when `sound3D` is `true`.
members.pan: Stereo pan. `-1.0` is fully left, `0.0` is centre, `1.0` is fully right. Panning has no effect when `sound3D` is `true`.
members.pause: Control the playback state of the sound. `play()` starts or resumes from the current position, `pause()` freezes playback at the current position, and `stop()` resets the position to the beginning.
members.play: Control the playback state of the sound. `play()` starts or resumes from the current position, `pause()` freezes playback at the current position, and `stop()` resets the position to the beginning.
members.protectVoice: If `true`, SoLoud will never steal this voice when all voice slots are occupied. Use for critical audio (e.g. player death sounds) that must always play.
members.seek: Jump to a specific position in seconds within the audio clip. Has no effect if no clip is loaded.
members.setInaudibleBehavior: Controls what SoLoud does when this voice becomes inaudible (volume reaches zero or the source is out of range).
members.sound3D: When `true`, the sound is rendered in 3D space relative to the active camera. The entity's world position is used as the source position. When `false`, the sound is a standard stereo/mono clip with no positional information.
members.speed: Playback speed (pitch) multiplier. `1.0` is normal, `2.0` plays at double speed (one octave up), `0.5` plays at half speed (one octave down).
members.stop: Control the playback state of the sound. `play()` starts or resumes from the current position, `pause()` freezes playback at the current position, and `stop()` resets the position to the beginning.
members.volume: Master volume for this source. A value of `1.0` is full-volume, `0.0` is silent. Values above `1.0` are allowed but may clip the audio output.

Sphere.description: A bounding sphere defined by a `center` point and a `radius`. Used for fast intersection tests and as a coarse culling primitive.

members.contains: Returns `true` if `point` is inside (or on) the sphere.
members.intersects: Overlap test against another sphere, AABB, OBB, plane, or a point.
members.merge: Expands this sphere to also enclose `other`.
members.toString: Returns a human-readable string like `"Sphere(center=(0,0,0), radius=1)"`.

Sprite.description: `Sprite` is the primary class for 2D images and sprite sheets. It renders a textured quad, supports texture atlas frames for manual sprite selection, and provides a simple frame animation player for looping sequences.

members.addFrame: Registers a named frame in the sprite sheet. Frames are used by setFrame and startAnimation.
members.createSprite: Builds the quad geometry and uploads it to the GPU. Optional in most cases — the mesh system rebuilds sprites automatically — but useful in C++ when you need the geometry immediately. Not bound to Lua.
members.flipY: Flips the texture vertically. Useful when loading textures from APIs that use a top-left origin (e.g. some framebuffer captures).
members.getOccluder2D: Attaches an Occluder2D component to the sprite's entity if one does not already exist, then returns an `Occluder2D` handle for configuration. The default `AUTO_QUAD` shape uses the sprite's mesh bounds, so it is the quickest way to make a sprite cast shadows from Light2D.
members.height: Physical size of the rendered quad in world units. If both are zero, the sprite uses the texture dimensions automatically after `createSprite()`.
members.pauseAnimation: Freezes the animation at the current frame. Call resumeAnimation to continue.
members.pivotPreset: Sets the pivot (origin) point used for position placement and rotation. See PivotPreset.
members.removeFrame: Removes a registered frame by ID or name.
members.resumeAnimation: Resumes a paused animation from where it was stopped.
members.setFrame: Selects the registered frame with the given ID or name. You can call this while configuring a new sprite, before its geometry has been built.
members.setSize: Sets both width and height in a single call. Equivalent to calling `setWidth` and `setHeight` separately.
members.setTextureRect: Restricts rendering to a sub-region of the texture using UV coordinates. Divide pixel x/width by the texture width and pixel y/height by the texture height. This setter applies immediately and cancels any pending frame selection waiting for texture dimensions. `getTextureRect()` returns the currently applied UV rectangle.
members.startAnimation: Plays a frame animation. Time values are in milliseconds.
members.stopAnimation: Stops the animation and resets to the first frame of the sequence.
members.textureRect: Defines the sub-rectangle of the texture to display in UV coordinates, where `Rect(0, 0, 1, 1)` covers the full texture. Use addFrame and setFrame for pixel-based atlas regions.
members.textureScaleFactor: Insets the UV rectangle by this many texels on every side, `0.0` by default. A small value such as `0.5` pulls the sampled area away from the edges of a packed atlas cell, hiding the neighbouring pixels that bilinear filtering would otherwise bleed in.
members.width: Physical size of the rendered quad in world units. If both are zero, the sprite uses the texture dimensions automatically after `createSprite()`.

SpriteAnimation.description: Cycles through a sequence of texture atlas frames on its target Sprite, creating flip-book-style 2D animation. This is distinct from skeletal animation (Animation); `SpriteAnimation` only advances the active frame of a sprite sheet.

System.description: `System` is a virtual platform-abstraction layer. It provides screen dimensions, file-system paths, virtual keyboard control, fullscreen management, and persistent key-value storage. You access it via `System::instance()` in C++ or the global `System` table in Lua.

members.getAssetPath: Returns the root path for read-only assets bundled with the project: the project's assets directory in the editor, and the `assets` folder beside the executable in an exported build. Prepend this to asset file names when opening files directly from C++. In Lua and the high-level C++ loaders (`setTexture`, etc.), paths are automatically resolved relative to the asset root.
members.getDirSeparator: Returns the platform path directory separator: `'/'` on Unix/macOS/iOS/Android/Web, `'\\'` on Windows.
members.getImportPath: Returns the directory holding the glTF conversions of FBX models: the project's `.doriax/imported` folder in the editor. It is empty in an exported build, where each conversion sits beside its FBX's path as `<name>.fbx.glb`. See 3D Graphics — FBX models.
members.getLuaPath: Returns the base path prepended when Lua `require()` looks for script modules and when a `ScriptComponent` entry is loaded: the project's Lua directory in the editor, and the `lua` folder beside the executable in an exported build.
members.getSampleCount: Returns the MSAA sample count configured for the current graphics backend (e.g. 1, 2, or 4). Useful when creating render targets that must match the main framebuffer.
members.getScreenWidth: Physical screen (window) dimensions in pixels. These may differ from Engine::canvasWidth / canvasHeight when a scaling mode other than `NATIVE` is active.
members.getShaderPath: Returns the directory holding compiled `.sdat` shader binaries, and the root for `shader://` paths: the project's `shaders` folder in the editor, and `assets/shaders` beside the executable in an exported build. The folder name is fixed, not configurable.
members.getUserDataPath: Returns a writable per-user data directory (Documents on iOS, internal storage on Android, `%AppData%` on Windows, `~/.local/share` on Linux). Use for save files and configuration.
members.isFullscreen: Query and control fullscreen mode. On desktop platforms, `requestFullscreen()` typically toggles borderless fullscreen; on web, it requests the Fullscreen API. Has no effect on mobile (always fullscreen).
members.isTouchDevice: Returns `true` when touch is the main input, as on phones and tablets. Android and iOS always report it. On the web the browser decides from its primary pointer, so a phone reports `true` and a laptop with a touch screen and a mouse reports `false`. Desktop platforms report `false`, and the editor reports `true` while touch simulation is on.
members.quit: Closes the application. The shutdown happens after the current frame ends, so it is safe to call from a button callback or any other script code, and `Engine::onShutdown` still runs before the app goes away.
members.requestFullscreen: Query and control fullscreen mode. On desktop platforms, `requestFullscreen()` typically toggles borderless fullscreen; on web, it requests the Fullscreen API. Has no effect on mobile (always fullscreen).
members.showVirtualKeyboard: Displays the platform's on-screen keyboard with `text` as the initial input buffer. Has no effect on desktop platforms. On iOS/Android, raises the software keyboard and fires `Engine::onCharInput` for each key typed.

Terrain.description: Generates and renders a heightmap-based terrain mesh using a chunked LOD (Level of Detail) approach. The terrain is built from a greyscale heightmap texture where brighter pixels correspond to higher elevation. Up to three blend maps control how up to nine detail layers are mixed over the base texture, three layers per blend map. A layer blends its colour alone, or carries its own PBR surface — see TerrainSurfaceLayer.

members.createTerrain: Explicitly builds the terrain geometry and GPU buffers after its source properties have been configured. This method is C++ only and is normally optional because the mesh system builds and rebuilds terrain automatically.
members.foliageDistanceScale: Multiplies the draw distance and min distance of every foliage layer, for a quality setting: `0.5` draws foliage half as far, `1` as authored. Negative values clamp to `0`, which hides the foliage. It applies on the next frame, is not saved with the scene, and the editor's foliage preview ignores it.
members.getNumLayers: How many layers the terrain currently holds, painted or empty.
members.getSurfaceLayer: Replaces or reads one whole layer, maps and factors together. `getSurfaceLayer` returns a copy, so editing it changes nothing until it is passed back to `setSurfaceLayer` — read, change, write.
members.levels: Depth of the LOD quadtree. Each level halves the node size, so the leaf node covers `size / (rootGridSize * 2^(levels-1))` world units — more levels means finer geometry near the camera, not a longer view distance.
members.maxHeight: The maximum elevation in world units corresponding to a fully white (255) heightmap pixel.
members.removeSurfaceLayer: Removes a layer. Blend map channels are positional, so every later layer moves down one channel — onto the paint the removed layer left behind. Only removing the last layer is lossless, which is all the Terrain Editor offers.
members.resolution: Number of grid segments per side of a single LOD node (not the heightmap size). Every node in the quadtree is drawn with this grid, so raising it densifies the geometry everywhere.
members.rootGridSize: The number of root quadtree nodes per side of the terrain. The coarsest node covers `size / rootGridSize` world units, so larger values start the quadtree with smaller nodes. At most 4, and capped by the terrain node budget together with `levels`: a larger value leaves the terrain unbuilt and logs an error.
members.setBlendMap: Sets a blend map. Each blend map weights three detail layers through its RGB channels: blend map 0 weights layers 0–2, blend map 1 layers 3–5, and blend map 2 layers 6–8. The one-argument form is blend map 0. Whatever weight the layers leave unclaimed goes to the base texture, so areas with no blend-map colour show the base alone.
members.setHeightMap: Sets the greyscale heightmap image. Each pixel's brightness maps linearly to height: black = 0, white = `maxHeight`. 8-bit and 16-bit images are both read (the editor's sculpting tools write 16-bit to avoid terracing). The image is stretched once over the terrain and sampled clamp-to-edge, so its outer texels define the terrain border.
members.setLayerFromMaterial: Fills a layer from a Material and turns on its PBR surface: base colour and factor, normal, metallic/roughness (assigned to both the roughness and metallic slots), occlusion, and the roughness and metallic factors.
members.setSurfaceLayer: Replaces or reads one whole layer, maps and factors together. `getSurfaceLayer` returns a copy, so editing it changes nothing until it is passed back to `setSurfaceLayer` — read, change, write.
members.setTextureLayer: Sets the colour of one detail layer, 0 to 8, and nothing else — a layer that carries a PBR surface keeps its other maps and factors. The vector of layers grows as needed, so assigning layer 4 also creates the empty layers below it; an unassigned layer renders as white.
members.size: World-space width and depth of the terrain in units. The terrain is always square.
members.textureBaseTiles: How many times the base and detail textures tile across the full terrain. Higher values produce smaller, more repetitive texture patterns; lower values stretch the texture.
members.textureDetailTiles: How many times the base and detail textures tile across the full terrain. Higher values produce smaller, more repetitive texture patterns; lower values stretch the texture.

Text.description: Renders a unicode string with a TrueType or OpenType font. `Text` produces a quad mesh from glyph data at the specified font size. It supports multi-line wrapping, fixed-size constraints, and exposes per-character layout information for custom cursor or selection rendering.

members.color: RGBA tint colour applied to all glyphs, in sRGB. It is stored linear internally, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one.
members.createText: Explicitly builds the text geometry and GPU buffers. This method is C++ only and is normally optional because the UI system builds and rebuilds text automatically. Use it when C++ code needs the geometry immediately.
members.fixedHeight: When `fixedWidth` is `false`, the text element automatically resizes its width to fit the rendered text. Same applies for height. Set to `true` to keep a fixed size and clip/wrap text instead.
members.fixedWidth: When `fixedWidth` is `false`, the text element automatically resizes its width to fit the rendered text. Same applies for height. Set to `true` to keep a fixed size and clip/wrap text instead.
members.flipY: Flips glyph texture coordinates vertically. The engine normally picks this automatically from the camera; calling the setter takes over and pins the value.
members.font: File path to a TTF/OTF font file, or a TrueType collection (`.ttc`). The `font` property and the overloads without an index read or write slot `0`, the main font. Setting the main font does not clear the fallback slots.
members.fontSize: The glyph render size in pixels (points at 72 DPI).
members.getAABB: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box of the rendered text in local or world space.
members.getAscent: Font metrics in pixels for the current `fontSize`. Useful for precise cursor or selection rendering.
members.getCharPosition: Returns the local-space pen position after the codepoint at `index`, in logical (string) order. Codepoints that shaping merged into a single cluster share one position.
members.getCharWidth: Returns the advance width of `codepoint` in pixels at the current font size, taken from the first font in the chain that covers it. Returns `0` when the font is not loaded yet.
members.getDescent: Font metrics in pixels for the current `fontSize`. Useful for precise cursor or selection rendering.
members.getLineGap: Font metrics in pixels for the current `fontSize`. Useful for precise cursor or selection rendering.
members.getLineHeight: Font metrics in pixels for the current `fontSize`. Useful for precise cursor or selection rendering.
members.getNumChars: Number of codepoints in the current string, excluding line breaks. This differs from `strlen` for multi-byte UTF-8 input, and from the number of glyphs drawn: shaping can merge codepoints into one ligature or expand one into several marks.
members.getWorldAABB: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box of the rendered text in local or world space.
members.maxTextSize: Number of characters the vertex buffer is preallocated for. It is not a limit: a longer string grows the buffer automatically and logs a warning. Raise it up front for text that is known to be long, to avoid the reallocation.
members.multiline: When `true`, the text wraps to multiple lines at the element's width boundary.
members.pivotBaseline: Controls the local-space pivot point. `pivotBaseline` moves the pivot to the text baseline; `pivotCentered` centres it on the bounding box.
members.pivotCentered: Controls the local-space pivot point. `pivotBaseline` moves the pivot to the text baseline; `pivotCentered` centres it on the bounding box.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures). An empty Texture draws the declared default. The texture is bound again without reloading the component. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame; a parameter with no value reads the scene's value under a scene default shader, else its declared default. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `ui` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`) the text draws with, such as `"shaders/outline.glsl"`. Its hooks see the font sample as `textureColor`. Empty (default) uses the scene's defaultUIShader, or the engine built-in. Changing it reloads the component, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. It is the `shader` field of UIComponent; see Custom Shaders.
members.text: The string to render. Supports UTF-8 encoded unicode.

TextEdit.description: An interactive single-line text input field. `TextEdit` composes an Image background, a Text display layer, and polygon overlays for the cursor and text selection highlight. It handles keyboard input, clipboard operations, cursor navigation, and optional password masking.

members.cursorBlink: Visual properties of the cursor caret. `cursorBlink` is the on/off period in seconds.
members.cursorColor: Visual properties of the cursor caret. `cursorBlink` is the on/off period in seconds.
members.cursorIndex: Current insertion-point position in the string, not on screen (0 = before the first character, `getNumChars()` = after the last).
members.cursorWidth: Visual properties of the cursor caret. `cursorBlink` is the on/off period in seconds.
members.disabled: When `true`, the field ignores keyboard and pointer events.
members.getTextObject: Returns the child Text entity used for rendering the input content.
members.maxTextSize: Maximum allowed number of characters. `0` means no limit.
members.password: When `password` is `true`, each character is displayed as `passwordChar` (default `'*'`). The actual text is still accessible via `getText()`.
members.placeholder: Ghost text displayed when the field is empty. Typically a prompt like `"Type here…"`.
members.selectionColor: Background colour of the text selection highlight polygon, in sRGB. The default is a translucent blue.
members.setSelection: Programmatically set or query the text selection. `anchor` is the fixed end of the selection; `focus` is the cursor end that moves with keyboard navigation. Pass equal values to collapse the selection to a cursor.
members.text: The current content of the input field.
members.textColor: RGBA tint colour applied to the input text glyphs.
members.textFont: Path to the TTF/OTF font file used by the inner Text. Falls back to the built-in fonts for codepoints it does not cover, see Text.font.

Texture.description: Represents a GPU texture resource. `Texture` supports 2D textures, cube maps, and framebuffer textures, covering the full range from loading a simple PNG file to driving a render-to-texture pipeline.

members.alphaBorder: Linear filtering also reads the color of fully transparent pixels next to visible ones, which image editors often save as black, and shows it as a grey or dark outline around the image. With the fix, those pixels take the color of their visible neighbors when the file loads, up to 4 pixels out. Alpha and visible pixels do not change.
members.destroy: Releases the GPU resource and removes the texture from the pool. After calling this, the texture object is empty.
members.empty: Returns `true` if no path, data, or framebuffer has been assigned to this texture.
members.getHeight: Returns the pixel dimensions of the loaded texture. Returns `0` if the texture has not been loaded yet.
members.getId: Returns the internal cache key used to identify this texture in the pool. For an SVG source with a non-default svgScale, the id encodes the scale (`"icon.svg?svgScale=4"`) because each scale is a separate pool entry; use getPath when you need the plain file path.
members.getPath: Returns the file path associated with this texture. For cube maps, `index` selects the face (0 = front, 1 = back, 2 = left, 3 = right, 4 = up, 5 = down).
members.getWidth: Returns the pixel dimensions of the loaded texture. Returns `0` if the texture has not been loaded yet.
members.isCubeMap: Returns `true` if this texture is a cube map (six faces).
members.isFramebuffer: Returns `true` if this texture was created from a Framebuffer (render-to-texture).
members.isFramebufferOutdated: Returns `true` when the render target has been resized or recreated since the texture last bound it, so the caller knows to rebind.
members.isTransparent: Returns `true` if the texture image contains pixels with alpha below `1.0`. Used internally by the engine to determine whether the owning mesh should be rendered in the transparent pass.
members.load: Forces an immediate CPU-side load of the texture data from disk. This is normally not required because loading is deferred, but you can call it to pre-warm assets during a loading screen.
members.magFilter: `minFilter` applies when the texture is rendered smaller than its native resolution (minification). `magFilter` applies when it is rendered larger (magnification). Only `NEAREST` and `LINEAR` are valid values for `magFilter`.
members.minFilter: `minFilter` applies when the texture is rendered smaller than its native resolution (minification). `magFilter` applies when it is rendered larger (magnification). Only `NEAREST` and `LINEAR` are valid values for `magFilter`.
members.releaseData: Frees the CPU-side pixel data after it has been uploaded to the GPU. Reduces memory usage on platforms with limited RAM. The texture remains valid for rendering.
members.releaseDataAfterLoad: Frees the CPU-side pixel data as soon as the texture reaches the GPU. `true` by default, but textures built from a TextureData keep their pixels: the `Texture(id, data)` constructor, setData and setCubeDatas all clear the flag, as does setFramebuffer. Setting it back on hands those pixels to the texture, so don't free them yourself. See releaseData to free the pixels on demand.
members.setCubeDatas: Creates a cube-map texture from six in-memory TextureData faces. The `id` is used as a pool cache key.
members.setCubeMap: Convenience overload that treats `path` as a directory containing six face images in the conventional naming format (`front`, `back`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`). Exact naming depends on the engine's convention.
members.setCubePaths: Loads a cube map from six individual image files. Typically used for skyboxes or environment reflections.
members.setData: Creates a texture from in-memory pixel data (TextureData). The `id` is an arbitrary string used as a cache key; using the same id for identical pixel data avoids uploading duplicates.
members.setFramebuffer: Points the texture at a render target so it can be sampled like any other texture. Also clears releaseDataAfterLoad, unlike the `Texture(Framebuffer*)` constructor, which leaves it set.
members.setId: Manually assigns a cache key without providing pixel data. Useful for referencing a texture that is already in the pool from another code path.
members.setPath: Sets the file path for a 2D texture. The file is not loaded immediately; loading is deferred to the first time the texture is needed for rendering.
members.svgScale: Rasterization scale for `.svg` path sources (`2.0` = twice the intrinsic resolution). Has no effect on raster images or framebuffer textures. Invalid values (zero or negative) snap back to `1.0`.
members.wrapU: Wrapping mode along the horizontal (U) and vertical (V) texture coordinates.
members.wrapV: Wrapping mode along the horizontal (U) and vertical (V) texture coordinates.

Tilemap.description: Renders a 2D tile grid as batched geometry. `Tilemap` works with two concepts:

members.clearAll: Removes all tiles and all rect definitions in one call.
members.clearRects: Removes all rect definitions. Tiles keep their rect IDs, so they stop drawing until rects with those IDs are added again.
members.clearTiles: Removes all tile instances. The rect definitions are preserved.
members.createTilemap: Explicitly builds or rebuilds the tilemap's geometry and GPU buffers. Configure the texture, rects, and tiles first, then call this method if C++ code needs the geometry immediately. It is not bound to Lua; the mesh system builds and rebuilds tilemaps automatically during rendering. Adding, removing, or clearing rects and tiles, and setting `textureScaleFactor` or `reserveTiles`, marks the tilemap to be rebuilt on the next frame.
members.findRectByString: Look up the integer ID of a rect or tile by name. Returns `-1` if not found.
members.findTileByString: Look up the integer ID of a rect or tile by name. Returns `-1` if not found.
members.getHeight: Returns the overall pixel dimensions of the tilemap bounding box (the extent covered by all placed tiles).
members.getRect: Returns a reference to the TileRectData struct for the given rect. Editing the struct in place does not rebuild the tilemap. To change a frame at runtime, call addRect again with the same ID.
members.getTile: Returns a reference to the TileData struct for the given tile. Editing the struct in place does not rebuild the tilemap. To move, resize, or remap a tile at runtime, call addTile again with the same ID.
members.getWidth: Returns the overall pixel dimensions of the tilemap bounding box (the extent covered by all placed tiles).
members.removeRect: Removes an atlas-frame definition. Tiles that used the removed rect stop drawing. Rects with higher IDs move down by one, and the tiles that used them follow, so they keep their image.
members.reserveTiles: Pre-allocates GPU buffer space for this many tiles. If you know the maximum tile count in advance, set this before the tilemap is first built to avoid mid-game reallocations. Changing it later rebuilds the tilemap.
members.textureScaleFactor: Insets each tile's UV rectangle by this many texels on every side, `0.0` by default. A small value such as `0.5` keeps bilinear filtering from bleeding neighbouring tiles of the atlas into the edges of a tile. It is only exact while the texture keeps its size: the `RESIZE` texture strategy blurs the bleed further into the tiles.

TimedAction.description: Base class for all fixed-duration tweens. `TimedAction` drives a single value from `0.0` to `1.0` over a specified number of seconds, optionally with an easing curve. Concrete subclasses (AlphaAction, ColorAction, PositionAction, RotationAction, ScaleAction) apply that interpolated value to a specific property of the target object.

members.duration: Length of the tween in seconds.
members.getTime: `getValue()` returns the current eased output value in `[0, 1]`. `getTime()` returns the current elapsed time in seconds.
members.getValue: `getValue()` returns the current eased output value in `[0, 1]`. `getTime()` returns the current elapsed time in seconds.
members.loop: When `true`, the tween restarts from the beginning after completing.
members.pingPong: When `true`, the tween plays to the end and then back to the start, so one pass takes twice the duration. With loop it goes back and forth for good, which makes a floating bob a single `PositionAction`. The easing applies both ways.
members.setFunctionType: Apply an easing curve to the tween. See EaseType for available values.

members.color: The tint multiplied with the widget's texture, as linear RGBA — not sRGB.
members.shader: The project-relative path of the `ui` shader file or shader graph the element draws with; empty uses the scene's defaultUIShader, else the engine built-in. Set `needReload` after changing it. `shaderUniforms` and `shaderTextures` hold the values and textures of its parameters by name. Image, Text and Polygon set all three through `setShader`, `setShaderUniform` and `setShaderTexture`. `shaderRender` is the compiled shader the element draws with.

UILayout.description: Base class for all UI elements. `UILayout` extends Object with a pixel-based sizing and anchor system that lets widgets automatically resize and reposition relative to their parent container or the screen edges.

members.anchorOffsets: Pixel margins from the anchor points. For a `FULL_LAYOUT` preset with a 10-pixel margin, set all offsets to `10`.
members.anchorPoints: Normalised values in `[0, 1]` defining where each edge of this element is attached within the parent. For example, `(0, 0, 0, 0)` pins the top-left corner; `(0, 0, 1, 1)` stretches to fill the parent.
members.anchorPreset: Applies a AnchorPreset that sets `anchorPoints` automatically.
members.height: Pixel dimensions of the UI element. Only used when the anchor configuration does not stretch the element.
members.ignoreScissor: When `true`, this element is not clipped to the parent's scissor rectangle. Use for tooltips or overlays that must extend beyond a scrollable container.
members.pivot: The point the element scales and rotates around, as a share of its size: `(0, 0)` is the top-left corner (the default), `(0.5, 0.5)` the center and `(1, 1)` the bottom-right corner. It does not move the element: the position stays the top-left corner of the unscaled element, so anchors and layouts are unaffected. `getWorldPosition()` returns where the top-left corner is after scaling and rotation.
members.positionOffset: An additional pixel offset applied to the final computed position. Useful for fine-tuning placement without modifying the anchor configuration.
members.usingAnchors: When `false`, the element is positioned using the standard 3D transform from Object rather than the anchor system.
members.width: Pixel dimensions of the UI element. Only used when the anchor configuration does not stretch the element.

UserSettings.description: A cross-platform key-value store for persistent user preferences. Values survive app restarts and are stored in a platform-appropriate location (e.g. `SharedPreferences` on Android, `NSUserDefaults` on iOS, a settings file on desktop platforms).

members.removeKey: Deletes a key and its associated value from persistent storage.

Vector2.description: A 2D vector with `float` components `x` and `y`. Used extensively for 2D positions, sizes, UV coordinates, and directions throughout the engine.

members.crossProduct: Returns the 2D cross product (scalar), which equals the signed area of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors. Positive means `rkVector` is to the left of this vector.
members.distance: Distance between this vector and `rhs`. `squaredDistance()` is cheaper and useful when you only need to compare distances.
members.dotProduct: Returns the dot product (`x*vec.x + y*vec.y`). Useful for projections and angle calculations.
members.isValid: Returns `false` if any component is NaN or infinite.
members.length: `length()` returns the Euclidean magnitude `√(x² + y²)`. `squaredLength()` skips the square root for cheaper comparisons.
members.lerp: Linear interpolation from `*this` toward `target` by factor `t`. `t = 0` returns `*this`, `t = 1` returns `target`, and values outside `[0, 1]` extrapolate. See Vector3 lerp for following a target at any frame rate.
members.makeCeil: Component-wise minimum (`makeFloor`) or maximum (`makeCeil`) with `cmp`, applied in-place.
members.makeFloor: Component-wise minimum (`makeFloor`) or maximum (`makeCeil`) with `cmp`, applied in-place.
members.midPoint: Returns the midpoint between this vector and `vec`.
members.moveTowards: Returns `*this` moved toward `target` by at most `maxDistanceDelta`, never past it. See Vector3 moveTowards. On a velocity it gives a steady acceleration toward a wanted speed:
members.normalize: `normalize()` scales the vector in-place to unit length and returns a reference to `*this`. `normalized()` returns a new normalised copy without modifying the original.
members.normalizeL: Normalises in-place and returns the original length. Combines normalisation with a length query in a single pass.
members.normalized: `normalize()` scales the vector in-place to unit length and returns a reference to `*this`. `normalized()` returns a new normalised copy without modifying the original.
members.perpendicular: Returns a vector perpendicular to this one (rotated 90° counter-clockwise).
members.reflect: Reflects this vector about `normal`. `normal` should be a unit vector.
members.squaredDistance: Distance between this vector and `rhs`. `squaredDistance()` is cheaper and useful when you only need to compare distances.
members.squaredLength: `length()` returns the Euclidean magnitude `√(x² + y²)`. `squaredLength()` skips the square root for cheaper comparisons.
members.toString: Returns a human-readable string representation like `"Vector2(1.000000, 2.000000)"`.

Vector3.description: A 3D vector with `float` components `x`, `y`, and `z`. The primary type for 3D positions, directions, normals, colours (RGB), and velocity in Doriax.

members.absDotProduct: Returns the absolute value of the dot product. Useful for axis-aligned overlap tests.
members.crossProduct: Returns the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both `*this` and `v`. The result follows the right-hand rule.
members.distance: Distance between this point and `rhs`. Use `squaredDistance()` when only relative comparisons are needed.
members.dotProduct: Scalar dot product `(x*v.x + y*v.y + z*v.z)`. Returns the cosine of the angle between two unit vectors.
members.isValid: Returns `false` if any component is NaN or infinite.
members.length: `length()` returns the Euclidean magnitude `√(x² + y² + z²)`. `squaredLength()` omits the square root for cheaper magnitude comparisons.
members.lerp: Linear interpolation from `*this` toward `target` by factor `t`. `t = 0` returns `*this`, `t = 1` returns `target`, and values outside `[0, 1]` extrapolate. Unlike moveTowards, the step is proportional to the remaining distance, so the motion slows down as it gets close.
members.makeCeil: Component-wise minimum (`makeFloor`) or maximum (`makeCeil`), applied in-place. Useful for AABB calculations.
members.makeFloor: Component-wise minimum (`makeFloor`) or maximum (`makeCeil`), applied in-place. Useful for AABB calculations.
members.midPoint: Returns the midpoint between this vector and `v`.
members.moveTowards: Returns a point moved from `this` toward `target` by at most `maxDistanceDelta`. It never overshoots: once the remaining distance is within `maxDistanceDelta`, `target` is returned exactly. Pass `speed deltatime` as `maxDistanceDelta` for frame-rate independent movement. This is the preferred way to move toward a target, since the naïve `direction speed deltatime` overshoots when the step is larger than the remaining distance (for example on the first, large deltatime frame). A negative `maxDistanceDelta` moves away from `target`. Equivalent to Unity's `Vector3.MoveTowards` and Godot's `Vector3.move_toward`.
members.normalize: `normalize()` scales the vector in-place to unit length. `normalized()` returns a new unit-length copy.
members.normalizeL: Normalises in-place and returns the original magnitude in a single operation.
members.normalized: `normalize()` scales the vector in-place to unit length. `normalized()` returns a new unit-length copy.
members.perpendicular: Returns an arbitrary vector perpendicular to this one. Useful when you need a tangent without a reference direction.
members.reflect: Reflects this vector about `normal` (a unit vector). Equivalent to `v - 2 dot(v, n) n`.
members.squaredDistance: Distance between this point and `rhs`. Use `squaredDistance()` when only relative comparisons are needed.
members.squaredLength: `length()` returns the Euclidean magnitude `√(x² + y² + z²)`. `squaredLength()` omits the square root for cheaper magnitude comparisons.

Vector4.description: A 4D vector with `float` components `x`, `y`, `z`, and `w`. Used for RGBA colours, homogeneous coordinates, and quaternion-adjacent math inside the engine.

members.divideByW: Divides `x`, `y`, and `z` by `w` in place, the perspective divide that turns homogeneous clip-space coordinates into NDC. `w` keeps its value.
members.dotProduct: Returns the 4D dot product `(x*vec.x + y*vec.y + z*vec.z + w*vec.w)`.
members.isNaN: Returns `true` if any component is NaN.
members.isValid: Returns `false` if any component is NaN or infinite.
members.lerp: Linear interpolation from `*this` toward `target` by factor `t`. `t = 0` returns `*this`, `t = 1` returns `target`, and values outside `[0, 1]` extrapolate. Blends two colours, for example `red:lerp(blue, 0.5)`.
members.moveTowards: Returns `*this` moved toward `target` by at most `maxDistanceDelta`, never past it. See Vector3 moveTowards. On a colour it gives a fade at a steady rate:

Water.description: A water surface: a flat grid at the entity's height, displaced by Gerstner waves and shaded with scrolling ripples, sky or planar reflections, refraction of the scene behind it, shore and crest foam, and a fade seen from below the surface. Constructing a `Water` attaches a `WaterComponent` to the entity. Water has its own render path, so it is not a Mesh and needs no material, texture, or camera wiring.

members.buoyancy: `buoyancy` lets the water float the dynamic bodies whose Body3D buoyancy is above `0`; turn it off for water that is only for show. `buoyancyDepth` gives the water a bottom: a body whose centre of mass goes deeper than that below the surface no longer floats in it. `0` has no bottom.
members.buoyancyDepth: `buoyancy` lets the water float the dynamic bodies whose Body3D buoyancy is above `0`; turn it off for water that is only for show. `buoyancyDepth` gives the water a bottom: a body whose centre of mass goes deeper than that below the surface no longer floats in it. `0` has no bottom.
members.caustics: Brightness of the sunlight patterns on the floor seen through the water; `0` turns them off. `causticsScale` is the world size of one cell of the pattern. They need refraction and depthEffects, are brightest in shallow water, and scale with the directional lights reaching the surface.
members.causticsScale: Brightness of the sunlight patterns on the floor seen through the water; `0` turns them off. `causticsScale` is the world size of one cell of the pattern. They need refraction and depthEffects, are brightest in shallow water, and scale with the directional lights reaching the surface.
members.crestFoam: `foamColor` is in sRGB. `shoreFoam` is the water depth the shore foam covers (needs depthEffects); `crestFoam` (`0`–`1`) is how much of the surface breaks into whitecaps, `0` for none. See Rendering Pipeline — Foam for how the foam is drawn.
members.deepColor: The water colour, in sRGB (stored linear, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one). Shallow water takes `shallowColor` and turns to `deepColor` as it deepens; `depthFade` is the depth in world units where the deep colour takes over. Shallower water is lighter and clearer.
members.depthEffects: Uses the scene depth for shore foam, soft edges where the water meets geometry, and the shallow-to-deep tint. The depth comes from SSR or SSAO when the scene already has one of them on; otherwise the engine adds a depth pre-pass for the water. Only the main camera has the scene depth.
members.depthFade: The water colour, in sRGB (stored linear, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one). Shallow water takes `shallowColor` and turns to `deepColor` as it deepens; `depthFade` is the depth in world units where the deep colour takes over. Shallower water is lighter and clearer.
members.foamColor: `foamColor` is in sRGB. `shoreFoam` is the water depth the shore foam covers (needs depthEffects); `crestFoam` (`0`–`1`) is how much of the surface breaks into whitecaps, `0` for none. See Rendering Pipeline — Foam for how the foam is drawn.
members.getHeight: The world height and the unit normal of the surface over the world point `(x, z)`, waves included. The result matches the surface the next frame draws, so calling it in `onUpdate` keeps a buoy, a boat without physics, or a camera on the waves:
members.getNormal: The world height and the unit normal of the surface over the world point `(x, z)`, waves included. The result matches the surface the next frame draws, so calling it in `onUpdate` keeps a buoy, a boat without physics, or a camera on the waves:
members.load: Builds the grid and loads the shaders now instead of on the next frame. Not needed in normal use: the render system loads a water the first time it updates.
members.planarReflection: Reflects the scene, not only the sky, like a Mirror: the scene is drawn a second time, at half resolution, from a camera reflected across the water plane. `reflectionDistortion` is how much the ripples bend the reflection.
members.receiveShadows: Shadows of the scene lights darken the sun glints and the light under the surface. Takes effect only when the scene has a shadow-casting light. Deep, clear water shows shadows only faintly, because most of its colour is reflected sky.
members.reflectionDistortion: Reflects the scene, not only the sky, like a Mirror: the scene is drawn a second time, at half resolution, from a camera reflected across the water plane. `reflectionDistortion` is how much the ripples bend the reflection.
members.reflectivity: `reflectivity` scales the reflection (sky, or the scene with planarReflection), `specularIntensity` scales the sun glints, and `roughness` (`0`–`1`) spreads the highlight: low values give sharp glints.
members.refraction: Shows the scene behind the water, bent by the ripples and tinted by the water it crosses (see shallowColor). The engine copies the scene once per frame for it. `refractionDistortion` is how much the ripples bend what is seen through.
members.refractionDistortion: Shows the scene behind the water, bent by the ripples and tinted by the water it crosses (see shallowColor). The engine copies the scene once per frame for it. `refractionDistortion` is how much the ripples bend what is seen through.
members.ripples: Small ripples come from a tiling normal map, sampled twice in two layers that drift across each other. An empty path restores the built-in ripple map. Give a custom map a mipmap filter so distant ripples do not shimmer.
members.roughness: `reflectivity` scales the reflection (sky, or the scene with planarReflection), `specularIntensity` scales the sun glints, and `roughness` (`0`–`1`) spreads the highlight: low values give sharp glints.
members.setShaderTexture: Sets a texture parameter the shader declares with `#pragma param texture2D` or `textureCube`, by name (see Textures); the surface and the underwater fade both bind it. An empty Texture draws the declared default. Changing it reloads the water. `getShaderTexture` returns the texture set, empty when none.
members.setShaderUniform: Values of the parameters the shader declares with `#pragma param`, by name. The surface and the underwater fade read the same values. Setting a value only rewrites the uploaded block, so it can run every frame. Same semantics as Mesh.setShaderUniform; see Custom Shaders — Shader parameters.
members.shader: Project-relative path of the `water` shader file (`.glsl`) or shader graph (`.shader`). One file fills both hooks of the water: `getColor` on the surface, and `getUnderwaterColor` on the fade of the underwater view. An empty path uses the scene's default water shader, then the built-in. Changing it reloads the water, and a shader that fails to build draws as the built-in one. The waves stay the engine's, so getHeight and buoyancy still match the surface. See Custom Shaders — Water shaders.
members.shallowColor: The water colour, in sRGB (stored linear, so the value read back is the sRGB form of the stored one). Shallow water takes `shallowColor` and turns to `deepColor` as it deepens; `depthFade` is the depth in world units where the deep colour takes over. Shallower water is lighter and clearer.
members.shoreFoam: `foamColor` is in sRGB. `shoreFoam` is the water depth the shore foam covers (needs depthEffects); `crestFoam` (`0`–`1`) is how much of the surface breaks into whitecaps, `0` for none. See Rendering Pipeline — Foam for how the foam is drawn.
members.size: `size` is the width (X) and depth (Z) of the surface, centered on the entity and scaled by its transform. `subdivisions` is the number of grid cells along each side, capped at `512`. Short waves need more cells to keep their shape; the grid has `(subdivisions + 1)²` vertices, so raise it only as far as the waves need. Changing either rebuilds the grid.
members.specularIntensity: `reflectivity` scales the reflection (sky, or the scene with planarReflection), `specularIntensity` scales the sun glints, and `roughness` (`0`–`1`) spreads the highlight: low values give sharp glints.
members.subdivisions: `size` is the width (X) and depth (Z) of the surface, centered on the entity and scaled by its transform. `subdivisions` is the number of grid cells along each side, capped at `512`. Short waves need more cells to keep their shape; the grid has `(subdivisions + 1)²` vertices, so raise it only as far as the waves need. Changing either rebuilds the grid.
members.underwater: When the main camera goes below the surface, inside the water's area, the scene fades into the water with distance, using the same colours and depth fade, unless the camera is in a WaterExclusion. With depthEffects off the fade is even, as if everything were `depthFade` away.
members.wakeArea: The wakes of the Water Exclusions moving across the water are kept in a square around what the main camera looks at, `wakeArea` world units on a side, in 256 × 256 texels: the default 64 resolves a quarter of a unit, enough for the foam along a small boat. A larger area reaches farther with coarser foam. The square moves with the camera without moving what it holds; a wake that leaves it is dropped. `wakeFade` is the seconds a wake takes to fade, foam and waves alike.

WaterExclusion.description: A volume that keeps Water out, like the inside of a boat. Inside it the water surface is not drawn, a camera sees no underwater fade, and dynamic bodies get no buoyancy, so cargo rests on the floor of a boat instead of floating on the sea outside. Constructing a `WaterExclusion` attaches a `WaterExclusionComponent` to the entity, and the volume moves, rotates, and scales with it.

members.center: The box or sphere in the entity's local space: `size` is its width, height, and depth, centred on `center`. A hull ignores them.
members.contains: Whether the world point is inside the volume, tested as buoyancy tests it. Gameplay that should agree with the water, like the air of a diver, can use it:
members.shape: A hull is convex, so a boat with a dip in its outline, like a catamaran, takes one volume per hull, each on its own mesh. Building a hull needs 3D physics, which projects have unless they turn `DORIAX_PHYSICS_3D` off (see Build Options).

WebPortal.description: The SDK of a web game portal, behind one API: ads, gameplay and loading events, and cloud saves. A web export builds in the portal chosen with Game Portal in the project's Web settings: CrazyGames, Poki, GameDistribution, Yandex Games or YouTube Playables. Without one, and on every other platform, the calls do nothing and ads and saves report errors.

members.gameplayStart: Tell the portal when the player is playing: start at play and on resume, stop at every break, such as menus, pauses, and the end of a level. Portals use it to time their ads. CrazyGames, Poki and Yandex Games use it; the others ignore it.
members.getEnvironment: Where the game runs, known once `onInitialized` fired. `isAvailable()` is true for `LOCAL` and `PORTAL`, when the SDK works.
members.getPortal: The portal this build includes, or `NONE`. It reflects the build, not where the page runs: see `getEnvironment()` for that.
members.happytime: Marks a happy moment, like a level completed or a record beaten. CrazyGames and Poki use it.
members.initialize: Loads the portal's SDK and starts it. Call it once at startup, as some portals pause or mute the game from the start. `onInitialized(environment)` reports where the game runs.
members.loadData: The cloud save of YouTube Playables, kept in the player's account as one string. `loadData()` reports `onDataLoaded(data)`, with an empty string when nothing was saved yet, or `onDataLoadFailed(message)`. `saveData()` reports only failures, through `onDataSaveFailed(message)`. YouTube refuses saves made before a `loadData()`.
members.loadingStart: Bracket loading screens. Call `loadingStop()` once the game can be played: Yandex Games and YouTube Playables require it. CrazyGames and Poki also use `loadingStart()`.
members.requestAd: Asks the portal for an ad: `MIDGAME` at a natural break, or `REWARDED` when the player chose to watch one for a reward. `onAdStarted` and `onAdFinished` report an ad that played, and `onAdError(type, code, message)` one that did not. Grant a reward only in `onAdFinished`.
